title: Souther adequacy report
description: How well a model's `example`s cover it. Emitted by `souther examples --format json`. A reader keys on `schemaVersion`, which is open until a release first ships it and frozen from then on. While it is open the schema it names may still be refined, a key made required included, because nothing outside this compiler has read a promise about it. Once it is frozen, every later schema of that version accepts every document any release of it accepted: a key added since is optional and a word added to an enumerated field is one no earlier document carried, so a document written before either existed is still a document of this version, and a change that removes, renames or requires anything raises the number instead. That is one direction: every object here is closed, so an older copy of this schema refuses a document carrying a key added since. A reader that has to accept newer documents wants the newer schema, not a higher number.

allOf.description: An open verdict names what it is open on, and a settled one is open on nothing. Written as a shape and not only as a sentence: the conformance corpus produced `undetermined` beside an empty array the day the field existed, and a description saying that cannot happen is a description a renderer can go on contradicting.

compilerVersion.description: The compiler that produced the report, or `unreleased` when it ran from class files.

status.description: The weakest status among the modules. `partial` means something could not be read, so an absent number is not evidence of a gap.

adequacy.description: Whether the rows satisfy the obligations the account derives, which is not what `status` says. What is owed is the model's — every obligation a derivation states is one a row is owed at, and no request narrows that — while what was measured decides whether the evidence to settle one was got at all. So `satisfied` is every obligation settled and none of them unmet, `not_satisfied` is one shown unmet, and `undetermined` is evidence that was not asked for or could not be established. A build that gates on this refuses `not_satisfied` and nothing else.

keptOpenBy.description: The facts keeping `adequacy` undetermined, one entry each. Empty for a settled verdict, `satisfied` or `not_satisfied` alike: a build refused over a gap has an answer whatever else went unmeasured, so what is here is what holds the word open and never a list of everything that fell short. Not `weakening`, which is a different question at a different unit — that one is about one measure or one module, its unit is the published kind, and it says each kind once. This one is about the verdict and its unit is a fact, so two things this document calls by the same word are two entries, and the entries are not folded on what they are printed as. The one fold there is happens before: two measures that went without the same fact went without one fact.

sources.description: What each source identity written elsewhere in this document is called, keyed on the identity. Every identity the document carries has an entry: every field defined by `sourceIdentity`, and the `subject` of a reason whose `scope` is `source`, which is an identity for that scope alone and so is spelled as the subject of any other. Said by pointing at the definition rather than by listing the fields, because a list is what the next field to carry one is missing from. Not a list of what the compile was handed: a source this report says nothing about has no entry, so this says which files the report is about rather than which files were read. The names are the ones the same run's diagnostics use, which are chosen from the set of files in front of a reader and are neither stable across runs nor a key — which is why they are here and not in place of the identities.

sourceIdentity.description: A source as the compilation identifies it, written once here for every field that carries one. It is what the caller handed the file over as — a position in a list for a build, a document URI for an editor — and not a name to show a reader: what to call a file depends on which other files are in front of that reader, so it is neither stable across runs nor a key. `sources` says what each of these is called. A field that carries one says so by being defined here, which is what lets a reader find every one of them without a list of the places they appear.

ruleHandle.description: How a reader finds a rule, written once here for every field that carries one. A rule the author named is found by that name: a clause of an invariant they called something is `invariant Amount (cap)`, one they named nothing is counted from the top of the declaration as `invariant Amount #2`, a clause of an `ensures` is `ensures charge (refunded)`, and a clause stating one rule over every answer is `ensures charge`. A rule they wrote rather than named has no name to look up and is found by where it is: `comparison@billing.sou:14:22` in a source this document's `sources` table names, and `comparison@7:3` where the file is the reader's to know. Code this compile reads from somewhere it holds no file for is said by what reaches it — `comparison in `Money`, reached at billing.sou:14:22`, or `comparison in `Money`, reached at 7:3`, or `comparison in `Money`` where there was no position to give. The word in front of a place says what kind of rule it is, and is one of the words `ruleId.kind` uses for a rule with no name: `predicate@billing.sou:14:22`, `predicate@7:3`, `predicate in `Money`, reached at billing.sou:14:22`, `predicate in `Money`, reached at 7:3`, `predicate in `Money``, and `fork@billing.sou:14:22`, `fork@7:3`, `fork in `Money`, reached at billing.sou:14:22`, `fork in `Money`, reached at 7:3`, `fork in `Money``. These words are how an author acts on a rule and never what tells one rule from another — two arms of one `ensures` clause may name the same case — which is `ruleId`.

compositionBudget.description: A figure this compiler holds a piece of its own work to, which an author could raise. Which way it acted on a search — stopping it, or cutting short the plan it ran over — is the field it is written under.

workFigure.description: A figure this compiler holds a piece of its work to outside the composing of values: how far a walk writes a container out, how large a machine for the strings a rule admits may grow, how far one row is run or observed. Some are fixed and some are handed to a run.

figure.description: Any figure of this compiler's a reading was compared against and stopped at, by the name it is declared as: one the composing of values holds itself to, or one of the rest of this compiler's work. The two vocabularies share no word.

runSensitivity.description: Whether a wider run of this compiler could come to a different answer about one thing it fell short of. A wider run is the same sources, the same compiler build, the same dependencies and the same host, with one or more of the allowances this compiler stops under widened and none of them narrowed — an allowance being a figure it compared something against and stopped on: the steps a row is evaluated for, the depth a recursion may reach, the clock it is held to, the nodes an observation keeps, the combinations a measure walks, the states a pattern is built into. Whether a caller can set the figure today is not the question; several of them are constants, and which knobs exist is a fact about this month rather than about the stop. `may_change` does not promise that a wider run finishes the measure — a reading past one figure may be stopped by the next — it says the stop that produced this need not happen again. `unaffected` is the stronger of the two and the one to act on: no allowance widens it, so measuring the same model again with more allowed finds the same thing. Neither says anything about what a later version of this compiler could read, or about writing the model another way; both are outside what a run is. The host is not an allowance either: a stack that ran out and classes that would not link are met again by a wider run on the same machine, and a run on another machine is a different host rather than a wider run of this one.

adequacyOpening.description: One thing keeping the adequacy verdict undetermined, projected to what a document may say of it: the kind it is, and whether a wider run could answer it. Only one of the ways a verdict stays open is a measure going without something. A measure that could have found a gap and was never made weakens nothing, and neither does a point the rows are read out at where nothing could show a row can be written — whether one can be is a second question, settled from what showed it rather than from what the rows covered. So a list of what fell short says nothing at all about a model nobody has written rows for, or about a point nothing promised, while the verdict over each stays open. Every entry says what it is about: a document naming only the kind told a reader how many things held the verdict open and none of what they were.

anyOf.description: A measure the verdict rests on was never made, so a gap it could have found is one nobody looked for. Nothing fell short here, which is why it is not one of the words above: those say what a measurement went without, and this says there was no measurement.

The rows are read out, no row is at a point the model owes one at, and what was read to show a row can be written there did not come back. The obligation stays: what did not arrive is a showing, not the model taking the point back.

The same point, where this compiler declined to compose a candidate for it at all — a figure of its own decided that, which is why this is its own word beside `showing_stopped` and why a wider run may get past it.

The same point again, where nothing was stopped and nothing arrived: no showing was made, so there is no limit to raise and nothing to name. Told apart from the two above because a reader sent after what stopped it would be looking for something nobody met.

An obligation — a case of an input, a class of a position or a combination of two classes — every row of which reaches an `unreachable` the body states, and nothing proves the inputs there do not arise. The obligation is still counted and is not a gap: a row there is refused (E1911), so none can be written, and it is not met either. One entry per part of the body that states it, however many obligations rest on it; `about` is the behavior whose body that is.

A point a value at was shown, where something worked out on the way to it may stop a run on values this compiler does not say — a product of two values nothing bounds, a sum of decimals, a call to another behavior — so no run was shown to get there with it. The obligation is still counted and is not a gap: an author told to write a row there may be asked for one no run reaches. Added after this version shipped: a document written by an earlier release carries no such entry, and a point of this kind was written there as a gap.

kind.description: What kind of thing this is, in two vocabularies. A measure that went without something writes the word `weakening` already has for it, where one word covers more than one thing this compiler can meet — a pattern too large to build and a rule about a value made from another are both `rule_unread` — so this says which kind it was and not which of them. The six beside them are the ways a verdict stays open that no weakening covers. Two entries alike are two things rather than one said twice, whichever vocabulary they are in.

observedIn.description: The behaviors whose measurement the fact showed up in, for a fact several behaviors can share. An unsettled fork that two behaviors reach is one entry naming both, not two entries: `about` says what is unsettled and this says where it was met. Only the behaviors whose count left the fork out are here, not every behavior that reaches it. Ordered by module and then behavior. Absent where the kind has no behavior to name.

notMeasuredReason.description: What a measure nobody made was waiting for, in the words this document already writes wherever a measure has no number. Written only beside `not_measured`, and one entry per measure rather than one per reason: two measures both waiting on rows are two measures nobody made, and a model with one behavior unmeasured is not the same news as a model with forty.

weakening.description: What left this measurement weaker than its numbers look, one word per fact. Present exactly where something did, and absent where nothing did. This is what makes four status words carry five states: `unavailable` with a `reason` of `not measured` and no `weakening` is a measurement nobody asked for, and the same with a `weakening` is one that was asked for, started, and could not be finished. Beside a `partial` it says which reading fell short, which a reader used to have to find somewhere else on the page or not at all.

ruleStoppedReadingReason.description: A rule this compiler read and could not use, which is what both surfaces below share. Such a rule is at a position — so a position's reading is short of it — and it is a shortfall about the rule, so a question the rule raised stands on it. Written once because the two surfaces really do share it, and not because their vocabularies happen to look alike. `exact_values_too_costly` is what a reader is told where working the values out was more than this compiler does. It is one published word over two facts this compiler tells apart: one rule names a set of strings whose machine it will not make, which is about that rule; or every rule was made into the set it names and what those come to between them was not, which is about the answer and names no rule. Sharing a word is not sharing a capability — what a document may say about the second is not what it may say about the first — so a reader is told what stopped and never which rule to go and change, and which of the two it was stays this compiler's question. Schema 22 had `pattern_too_deeply_nested`, for a pattern nested more deeply than the reading goes; a document of that version may carry that word, nothing writes it now, and such a pattern is refused where it is checked, so no document is written of a program holding one. Schema 23 wrote `rule_about_an_element_of_several_sequences` where this writes `rule_about_an_element_of_several_containers`: the element it is about is a map's key or value as well as a list's or a set's element, and the word says so. `line_at_a_number_no_ratio_holds` is a line with no place, and `line_side_not_worked_out` is a line that is placed with a value beside it this compiler could not write out — two facts that call for looking at different things in the rule. `several_lines_in_one_rule` is a rule whose meaning was read in full and is several lines held together, where those lines are not drawn: what a closure states on each application it is handed, a statement one of whose relations is about something no row writes, or a clause, which has nowhere to hold where each of its lines decides what the clause comes to; nothing about what it states is unknown, so it is not `unsupported_syntax`. `relation_not_shown_to_reach_every_value` is a rule whose meaning was read in full and that relates the value at the position to another value nothing showed reaches every value there — the length of a string against a number that may be below nought, a value against what an operation answers of another — so some values at the position may settle the rule whatever the other holds, and which ones is not worked out; it is not `rule_relating_two_values`, which says the rule leaves every value at the position open. `relation_not_shown_reached_at_every_value` is a rule whose meaning was read in full and that relates the value at the position to another value, where a run may stop on the way to the rule on values this compiler does not say — an operator worked out before it on a value the rule reads — so not every value at the position is shown to get to the rule; it is not `relation_not_shown_to_reach_every_value`, where every value at the position gets to the rule and the other side is what falls short, so a reader looks at what the run works out before the rule and not at the other side. `relation_shown_over_a_region` is a rule whose meaning was read in full and that relates the value at the position to another value, whose classes there hold the values the relation was shown over and no others: the rest are shown on neither side of it, and the `leftOpen` beside the entry says which — those longer than a number of code points, past which nothing here wrote the other value out within the longest string or no value of the numbers the way ties their length to gets a run past an operation to the relation, those shorter than a number of code points for the second of those, and those the other side holds only through a code point normalization changes. It is not `relation_not_shown_to_reach_every_value`, which leaves the position no class of the rule's. `rule_relating_elements` is a rule recognised as saying how the elements of the container at the position stand to each other — no two of them alike, as a whole or at a field — where which containers it leaves is not worked out: a container composed at the position keeps it, and a container saying one element twice is still among what the position is taken to hold, so it is neither `unsupported_syntax` nor a rule read to the end. `unread_alternative_of_a_choice` is a rule offering an alternative this compiler does not read, where what the rule leaves at the position is what its alternatives leave together — its own word beside `unsupported_syntax` because the rule written at the position was read and places what it places, so an author told that one would rewrite a clause that is not the difficulty and the branch beside it would stand as unread as it was. `rule_meaning_not_read` is a rule placed at the position, a part of whose meaning this compiler did not read where that part is neither a form nothing takes apart, which is `unsupported_syntax`, nor what an operation answered, which is `rule_about_a_derived_value` — which case a called behavior answers, a clause of an invariant an attempt checks, a step of the reading not yet written, or more readings than this compiler makes — so where a line would fall is not known. `non_affine_product` is a rule whose comparison is over a product of two values neither of which is a constant, and `non_constant_divisor` one over a quotient by a value that is not a constant: the comparison depends on the position and on another number, nothing was made out of the position, and no line over them is one this compiler says — so neither is `rule_about_a_derived_value`, where there is an operation to read the rule back through. `non_constant_remainder_divisor` is the same for a remainder by a value that is not a constant, which has no period for a line over the values to be drawn at.

ruleOfferShortfallReason.description: What stopped the reading of a rule an offer of values got nothing from. Every word a reading that gave up on a rule writes, and `rules_not_read_at_all` beside them. That word keeps the meaning it has under `notRead`: the reading of the position never arrived at the rules written about it. It is written here for a clause nothing could type, where it names a rule because what an offer holds is the parts an author wrote, and it knows which part gave it nothing without any reading having got that far. A rule named beside it is not a rule that was read. The same clause is said in the same word under `notRead` at the position it stands at, so the two are one piece of news. Schema 23 admitted every word of `notReadReason` in this field; a document of that version carries only words this definition admits, since no other was ever written there, and narrowing what the field admits is what raised the version.

answerRealizationStoppedReason.description: What the answer at a position was short of, which is a fact about what the rules of that position come to between them and about none of them: the same rules met in another order would have been built. Its own vocabulary because it names no rule, so nothing written in one of these sends a reader to a clause. It is one word with something a document could name a rule for — `exact_values_too_costly` is written here and in `ruleStoppedReadingReason`, where it is a rule naming a set of strings whose machine this will not make — and the two stay apart because the fields do: a question carries one of each where it is short in both ways, and which field a word is in says which of the two facts it is about. `behavior_distinctions_too_costly` is the other half of the same kind and stays apart from `exact_values_too_costly` because the two bound different questions: that one is what the position admits coming out wider than its declarations leave it, and this one is what a behavior's own rules about the position tell apart, so a position answered to the letter by its declaration still carries it. Schema 12 had `questionStoppedReason`, one vocabulary over both facts, and with it `rule_not_interpreted_here`; a document of that version may carry that word, nothing writes it now, and the state it was written for is an answer that was not built.

notReadReason.description: Why a reading is short of the rules. `unsupported_syntax` is a rule that was read and could not be used — an expression the terms do not name; `rules_not_read_at_all` is a position whose rules the reading never arrived at — no rule is named because none was seen — with which limit stopped the walk neither recorded nor promised;  `unsupported_domain` is a comparison against values no line can be drawn on; `line_at_a_number_no_ratio_holds` is a comparison against values a line can be drawn on, read from end to end, whose line falls at a number this compiler has no exact representation for — a constant the rule is written with stands so near the end of the range of exponents that the place the line falls at, in the quantity's own units, cannot be named — its own word beside `unsupported_domain`, which says the values carry no order to draw a line on, because what an author looks at here is the constants of the rule and not the type of the position; `line_side_not_worked_out` is the same comparison with its line placed, where a value the order holds beside the line was not worked out — the host had no room to write its count out, or the number has no representation on the position's carrier — its own word beside `line_at_a_number_no_ratio_holds`, because the line is fine and what an author looks at is how far out the multiple of the position reaches; `rule_relating_two_values` is a rule read from end to end that relates the value at the position to another value rather than dividing the values there — to another position's, or to a value no position holds, such as what an operation looked up, an element a walk was handed, or the index it is at; `depth_limit` is the walk stopping after a count of steps, which nothing writes any more; `returns_to_a_declaration_already_read` is the input returning at this position to a declaration the path had already opened, which nothing writes any more: the return is where the listing of positions ends and what is under it is what is under that one, so a document of an earlier version may carry the word and a position is not left unread for it; `type_unresolved` is a type at the position that could not be worked out; `rule_about_a_derived_value` is a rule read and placed, written about a value an operation made from what stands at the position — where the values came from is known and what the rule says about the values here is not; `rule_about_an_element_of_several_containers` is a rule read and placed, written inside a block handed to more than one walk, so the name it reads an element under holds an element of a different container on each run — a list's or a set's element, or a map's key or value, and which of them the rule is about is not worked out — every position it may be about is told this one, including where some of those runs walk something the input has no part in, and unlike `rule_about_a_derived_value` nothing was made out of the element and there is no operation to read the rule back through; `rule_cuts_nothing` is a rule read from end to end whose quantity the position does not appear in, so there was no line in it to draw; `rule_answers_nowhere` is a rule read from end to end that every run reaching it stops in, an operation it is read through aborting first — a division by nought — so it states nothing on either side and there is no line or class in it — its own word beside `rule_cuts_nothing`, where a run gets past the rule and it comes out the same for every value; `rule_cuts_outside_what_the_quantity_holds` is a rule read from end to end whose line falls where the quantity it cuts never runs — a length compared against a negative — so there is no value either side of it and no class the position is divided into; `nothing_arrives_at_the_rules_line` is a rule read from end to end whose line the declarations do leave values at, while no row that arrives at the comparison holds one of them — what holds on the way there rules them out: the conditions taken, a guard shadowed by a stricter guard above it, and what a run got past working out, `a + 1` past only where `a` is below the greatest `Int` — so the classes the line would make hold nothing that gets there; `rule_never_turns_on_this_line` is a rule read from end to end that states several relations held together, one of whose lines is here — rows arrive at it, and wherever they do the rest of the rule already decides what it comes to, `Int.max(a, a + 1) > 5` where `a` passes five — so the line divides nothing a row could be held to; `nothing_arrives_at_the_relation` is a rule read from end to end that relates the value at the position to another value, while no row that arrives at the comparison takes the way to it — what holds on the way there rules them out, as for `nothing_arrives_at_the_rules_line` — its own word beside that one because the rule has no line of its own for the rows to miss, and beside `rule_relating_two_values` because nothing is left to work out; `rule_about_a_run` is a rule read from end to end whose line is drawn on a number taken over the values at this position rather than on any one of them — two of them either side of a total are on the line as surely as one is — so it divides the position into no classes while its border stands. `rule_about_a_remainder` is a rule read from end to end whose line is drawn on what a division by a written number leaves of a number made of the values at this position and others, so it divides none of them while its border stands on the remainder. `unresolved_case_pairing` is a rule read from end to end that draws a line, where each of the names it is between stands at more than one position — a field every case of a sum spreads is written once and a row writes it under one case — and which of those positions the line runs between is not worked out. `position_restricted_to_what_a_rule_admits` is a rule read from end to end that holds the position to the values it admits and places no end on them — a format states which strings stand there — where everything outside them is refused at construction, so there is no class away from them for a row to be owed at; what a reader acts on is that the value written here is one the rule admits, and whether the position is also divided is said by the classes rather than here. `rule_tells_nothing_apart` is a rule read from end to end, written about this position, that puts every value the position holds on one side of itself — a predicate over the strings here that no value satisfies, or that every value satisfies — so the model draws no line between any two of them and there is no second class for a row to be owed at; unlike `rule_cuts_nothing` the rule is about this position, and unlike `position_restricted_to_what_a_rule_admits` it leaves the values where it found them. `classes_not_composed` is every rule about this position having been read, with what they say not all sayable as one list of classes: a rule puts a line on the order the values are counted on or tells a set of them from the rest, and a class written in one of those cannot be written in the other, so a position both kinds reach has no single denominator here — unlike the two costly words nothing fell short, and a run allowed more meets it again; what the rules cut and where they part the position are unaffected and are reported as before. `behavior_distinctions_too_costly` is a behavior's rules about this position having been read, with working out what they tell apart costing more than this compiler does — its own word beside `exact_values_too_costly`, which is what the position admits coming out wider than its declarations leave it, because a position answered to the letter by its declaration still carries this one and an author told the other would go and simplify a declaration that was never the matter; the rules of a position are worked out as one group so that which of them a reader hears about does not follow the order they were walked in, and no rule of the group is named as the expensive one. `rule_cuts_nothing`, `rule_answers_nowhere`, `rule_cuts_outside_what_the_quantity_holds`, `nothing_arrives_at_the_rules_line`, `nothing_arrives_at_the_relation`, `position_restricted_to_what_a_rule_admits`, `rule_tells_nothing_apart` and `rule_relating_two_values` are facts about the model or about what this measure represents, and nothing is owed on their account; the rest are facts about the compiler. Schema 23 called `rule_relating_two_values` `unsupported_partition_shape`, and said it only of a rule relating two positions; a document of that version may carry the old word, and nothing writes it now. Schema 23 had `unsupported_traversal`, for values held inside something the walk did not reach into; a document of that version may carry that word, and nothing writes it now, because a map's values are read as its element the way a list's elements are.

location.description: Where on the quantity's order a point of a border is, which is what identifies it within its line. `at_the_line` is the value the rule wrote, which every line has one of. `beside_the_line` is the nearest value on one side of it, where the values there fall in another class than that value does — one side for a rule that orders the values, and both sides for one that names a value. `in_the_region` is a row away from the line, in the run on one side of it. Which of the four points each of these is follows from the place and from whether the rule holds there, and is published beside this rather than in it: a border can have two points in one role, and the role tells those two apart nowhere.

side.description: Which way from the line, on the order the quantity's own values sit on and never on the way the rule was written. Present for every place but the value the rule wrote, which is on the line and so on neither side of it.

allOf.description: Every place but the line's own value is on a side of it.

level.description: A level of whatever a line was drawn on, in the words of what it is a level of and never of where it was read. `on_a_carrier` is a place of the carrier a coordinate is ordered by, written the way that carrier writes one. `a_count` is a number the quantity itself counts to — how far two positions stand apart, or what an arithmetic form comes to — which is on no carrier. A quantity writes a level in the terms of where it was met, and a value owed once wherever it is read cannot take its words from one of them.

allOf.description: A level of a coordinate is on the order that coordinate is counted on; a number the quantity itself counts to is on none.

typeId.description: Which declaration a type is. The module and the name, because that pair is what a type's identity is: two modules may each declare a `Status` and they are two types. Not one word — a module name has dots in it, so a joined spelling cannot be taken apart again. A type the language declares has no module: it is one of a closed set the language fixes, and its name is its identity.

allOf.description: Only a declaration of a module has one to name.

carrier.description: Which order a level is counted on, said in this document's own words rather than in whatever a compiler calls one to itself. `ordinal` carries the enumeration and the cases it declares, because two enumerations are two orders however alike their cases count and where a case comes in the declaration is what the order is.

allOf.description: The enumeration and its cases are written exactly for an order a `data` of cases gives.

authoredLineId.description: One line of the model: which rule drew it, and which of that rule's lines it is. Which line is `which`, and it carries the rule together with whatever names a line of that kind of rule, because the kinds are not decomposed alike. Two lines of one rule at one place are told apart by what each says about its own value — `value >= 5 && value <= 5` puts a minimum and a maximum at five and they are two lines — which is `facts`. `narrowedWithin` is the declarations that took an end in: a bound another type narrowed is not the bound it narrows.

facts.description: What the rule placed on the values either side of what it wrote. A rule that orders them says which side its own value belongs to; one that names a value orders nothing either side of it and says no side at all, which is why `valueBelongsBelow` is written exactly where `singles` is false.

narrowedWithin.description: The declarations that took an end in, each by its identity and in their own order — a set, so which reading was met first does not move them. Always a declaration of a module: a type the language fixes narrows nothing.

thresholdOfADerivedValue.description: Which threshold of a computation cut at several places a point or a line is, for a total looked up in a table: it owes its ON and OFF points once for each threshold, and a threshold belongs to one computation, whatever number the bounds of two computations come to. `written_at` is the bound the comparison was written against, as the table holds it, and is one threshold however many places the computation is cut at. `cut_at` is the place the computation is cut at, for a comparison whose bound could not be told. `held_in` is the bound of a comparison that is no place of such a computation, told by the data it is written in: two calls of one helper given two tables read two thresholds however alike the bounds, while one table reached by two calls, or under another name, is one. `copies` names the computation. `heldIn` names the data the bound is read out of, which a `written_at` threshold carries too where its bound is read out of a table. Absent for a comparison cut at one place whose bound is held in no data.

heldIn.description: The data the bound is read out of, each as the location it is: the binding it is rooted at and the fields read from there, in one order. What a reader calls it is in the human report and is no part of which data it is.

bound.description: The number the comparison was written against.

quantity.description: The weighing of the positions the computation is cut on.

boundaryLineId.description: One line a row can be written at: where it was drawn, and which line of the model was drawn there. Both, because either alone names more than one line. One line of a type is drawn at every position the type stands at, and those lines share `line`; one rule draws several lines at one place, and those share `target`. Which reading of the model drew the line is not part of it, so a line one helper draws once per call is one line here. A comparison written in a body carries `placement` as well, which is how the points of the line drawn here are the points of the line its author wrote: one comparison put at one place facing its author's sides two ways — `check(a, 10)` and `check(20 - a, 10)` — is two lines here, because the run on one side of the place is one of the author's points in one and another in the other. Two of these are one line exactly when they are equal as JSON values.

placement.description: `placed` is a line shown to be a place of the author's line, with each of its own points (`point`) and the author's point it is (`authored`), or no `authored` where the reading cannot tell which of the author's sides it is on. `no_place_of_the_line` is a line a caller's choice draws between values the comparison comes out one way for. `not_shown` is a line where a caller's choice turns the comparison, which is not shown to be a place of the author's line or not to be one.

target.description: Where the line was drawn: the behavior whose input it is on, the quantity it cuts and the level it cuts it at.

quantityId.description: What a line cuts, by every part that tells one quantity from another: which shape it is, and what it weighs each of its terms by. A form is written over its terms, which way it runs included — one position's own values are that position weighed once, and how far two positions stand apart is the first weighed once less the second once — so `shape` is what tells one position's values from a form weighing that position once. The orders each term stands on are part of it as well: two quantities over one place that are read or measured on different orders are two. A count of the elements meeting something is no form and weighs no terms: `shape` is `count_of_elements`, and `counted` names which count it is in place of `terms`. So is a count of the different values those elements hold at one place: `shape` is `count_of_different_values`, and `counted` names it. A remainder of a form and a product of two numbers are no form either, and `counted` names them the way `boundaries[].axis` does.

shape.description: The same word `boundaries[].kind` writes for the line.

counted.description: Where `shape` is `count_of_elements`: the container whose elements are counted and what each is counted for meeting, as `#container [statement]`. Where it is `count_of_different_values`: the container, the place whose values are counted, and what an element is kept for meeting, as `#different container [place] where [statement]`. Absent for every other shape.

terms.description: Each term with its coefficient, in the order a form's terms are walked in, so one quantity is always written one way. No constant: a constant is part of the level.

coefficient.description: An exact number, written one way for one value.

termOrders.description: The order a value at the term's place is read on, and the order the number the term names is measured on. Either is absent where the term has none: nothing orders a container, which is read by what it holds.

termId.description: Which number a line is drawn on. A place is written in the spelling that says which kind each narrowing is, because the spelling an author reads can write two places alike that this compiler holds apart.

oneOf.description: The number a position holds.

A number an operation takes of what a position holds, together with whatever the call gave it beside that value, each by where it stands in the call: a quotient by two and a quotient by three are two numbers of one place.

value.description: An exact number, written one way for one value.

from.description: What the value the number is taken of was made from the one at `position`, where it was made into anything: the date there moved by `days`, which is defined for the dates from `defined_from` to `defined_to`. Absent where the number is taken of the value as it stands.

oneOf.description: A number an operation takes over a run of values, which no one position holds. `over` says where the values are read from.
Every value standing at one position inside one sequence.

What is computed of each element of one sequence: one value per element, each made of that element's own fields by `computation`. No position holds these values, so `elements` says where the elements stand and `computation` what is made of one of them. Where what is computed turns on where each element stands, `handed` says which end the walk was handed them from, since the same elements handed from the other end are another run; absent where it turns on no element's position.

Every node of a tree from the node at `root` down, each once: that node and the elements of the fields `through` of every node reached. Where `container` names fields of a node, the values are the elements of the container there in every one of those nodes instead. No position below the root holds these values, since a type that holds itself is not read again below it.

How many of the code points of the string a position holds are in a class: every one that is not whitespace, every one that is neither whitespace nor `separator`, or every one in `ranges`, each an inclusive pair of code points.
How many elements of the container a position stands inside hold there what the element under consideration holds. No one position holds it.

The least or the greatest of what the elements of the container `position` stands inside hold there, among the elements holding at `key` what the element under consideration holds there. One of the values at `position`, and not the one the element itself holds: no one position holds it.

through.description: The operation whose step of each value the end is taken of, as the day a date-time falls on is: the end is of those steps and not of the values.

oneOf.description: What the elements standing at `elements` come to, among the elements holding at `key` what the element under consideration holds there: the total of what `computation` makes of each, the same total from the last element that puts its number in place of the ones before (`put_by`), or the least or the greatest of it. The elements are every occurrence of the place, in one container or in the containers inside another put end to end. No one position holds it.

kept_by.description: The statement the elements gathered are kept by, where only some occurrences are: one that does not meet it is filed under no key. Absent where every occurrence is gathered. Two keepings of one place are two numbers.

key_by_case.description: Where the key is chosen by the case of the value at `subject`: an element is filed under what it holds at the `key` of the arm whose `taken` its case is, and two elements holding one value are one key whichever arm each was read by. `key` then spells the arms. Absent where every element holds its key at one place.

oneOf.description: What the elements standing at `elements` come to, among those holding at `key` what the input holds at `asked`: the total of what `computation` makes of each, the same total from the last element that puts (`put_by`), or the least or the greatest of it. The elements are every occurrence of the place, as for `gathered_under_its_key`. It is no number where no element holds the key, and no one position holds it.
What the code points of the string a position holds come to, each added as the number it is.
The code point the string a position holds has at `index` of its code points, counted from nought.

The step of a coarser order that the value a position holds falls in, as `operation` answers it: the day a date-time falls on. The step is the value's count over the operation's unit, floored toward the earlier step.

putBy.description: Where `gathering` is `total_from_the_last_put`: an element whose value at `subject` is of one of the cases `taken` puts its number in place of the ones before, and what a key comes to is the total of its elements from the last such the walk was handed. Which was handed last is the order and not the elements, so `handed` says which end the walk was handed them from: the same elements handed from the other end come to another number. Absent for every other gathering.

putByOfItsGathering.description: `put_by` is written exactly where the gathering is `total_from_the_last_put`: that gathering is not said without the elements that put, and no other gathering, nor a number gathered by none, has any. Stated once of every number a line is drawn on, rather than in each branch that writes a gathering, so the two numbers gathered under a key cannot come to say it two ways.

handed.description: Which end of the elements a walk whose number turns on their order was handed first: `as_written` from the first the row writes, `from_the_far_end` from the last of them.

elementComputation.description: What one element's number is made of: a sum of its fields each weighed by a number, a sum of products of its fields each weighed by a number, the choice between two such by a flag the element holds, the choice among them by which case a value of the element is, the choice between two by where the element stands, or several such choices added up. A field is named by its steps from the element, joined by dots, with a narrowing to a case written `@` and the case, and by the empty string where the element is itself the number. Terms are listed in the order the fields' names sort.

constant.description: An exact number, written one way for one value.

weight.description: An exact number, written one way for one value.

oneOf.description: The choice between two by where the element stands in the container it was walked from, counted from nought in the order the row writes them: `whenHolds` where the position, or what is left of it divided by `divisor` with the quotient floored, stands to `against` as `relation` says, and `otherwise` elsewhere. `divisor` is absent where the position is compared as it is. Which answer an element takes is fixed by the row and not by any value it holds.

The position times a number made of the element, and a number beside it: `perPosition` for each step of where the element stands in the container it was walked from, counted from nought in the order the row writes them, plus `base`. Two elements holding the same values come to different numbers.

The arm a `match` on a value of the element takes, tried in the order written: each arm by the place its name stands at, which is the value narrowed to the case the arm took, and what the element comes to there. `otherwise` is what an element no listed arm takes comes to, and is absent where the arms take every value.
Choices of the element added up, each at its weight, with a form beside them. Each choice is made for the element on its own. The choices are listed in one order made of them alone.

weight.description: An exact number, written one way for one value.

oneOf.description: A sum of products of the element's fields and of roundings of numbers made of it, each term at its weight, and a constant beside. A product names each of its fields once, in the order their names sort; a product of one field is that field. A rounding stands alone: `scale` is how many places it keeps, `mode` how it rounds, and `value` what it rounds. At least one term is a product of two fields or more, or a rounding. Terms are listed in the order their spellings sort.

constant.description: An exact number, written one way for one value.

scale.description: A whole number, written one way for one value.

mode.description: How it rounds, in this document's words: `half_up`, `half_even` and `half_down` to the nearer step, parting at an exact half up, to the even step, or down; `away_from_nought`, `toward_nought`, `toward_the_greater` and `toward_the_lesser` to the step that way.

weight.description: An exact number, written one way for one value.

operationId.description: A library operation: the alias the library is published under, and the operation under it. No `name` where what was applied is the namespace itself.

obligationId.description: What tells one thing a row is owed for from every other, which is not what a reader is shown. A key within this document: a `partition.obligations` entry carries it and so does every finding about one, and a consumer joins them on it. Which of the four points it is is not in here — a rule that names a value owes a row outside it on each side, so two of these can be the same `role` and the role tells them apart nowhere. What does is where the point is (`location`) and, for a line a declaration drew, the level and where a run stops (`stops`): a declaration's line read at two positions whose types stop the run in different places owes two runs at one level on one side. A comparison written in a body carries neither: the level and the far end of a run are where each call put the comparison, which is the reading's and not the author's, so a point of its line is one point however many places it is read at, and each reading says its own under `readings`.

stops.description: What settled where the run stops. `at_a_line` is a rule that put a line there, named by the line and the place it parts the values. `at_the_domain` is what every rule about the position leaves together, which is a place and no one rule. `at_the_order_end` is nothing stopping it, so the run goes as far as the order does.

allOf.description: A line that stopped the run is named by the line and the place it parts the values.
An end the declarations leave together is a place and how much of the quantity it is a place of.
An end nothing stopped is which way the run goes.
A line a comparison written in a body draws carries no level and no far end; every other line carries its level.
A point away from a declaration's line asks for a row in the run beside it, and where that run stops is part of what the point is. A point at a value of the quantity has no run.

obligations.description: What a set of obligations comes to: one entry per thing a row is owed for, once each however many positions read the line, with every reading of it. A behavior's account and the declarations' are two projections of one relation and are written in this one shape, so a consumer joins a finding to either by `obligationId`.

rule.description: The rule that drew the line this point is owed for. The handle and nothing else, where the `boundaries` entry for the same line writes the declarations that took its ends in beside it.

relation.description: How a row's value relates to what it is against, the word `boundaries[].items[].relation` uses.

disposition.description: What became of this obligation, which the evidence beside it is why. All four are in the count: whether a row is owed at a point is the model's answer, and nothing this compiler failed to read, compose or represent changes it. `unmet` says the absence is established, so it is a finding; what a build does about that finding is a separate question and is answered under `findings[].disposition`. `refuted` says the rules of the way to the point leave it no value, so there is no row to write and nothing to raise — it is the model's own answer and never a search that came back empty, and it is no finding. `undecided` says nobody could decide it and names the open questions under `undecidedAbout`.

undecidedAbout.description: Every question about this obligation that nothing answered, written where `disposition` is `undecided` and never elsewhere. Both can hold of one obligation, and they are lifted by different work: the first by rows being read, the second by this compiler being able to compose, keep or represent more than it does.

hit.description: Whether some row stands at the point, under any reading of it. Present exactly where `status` is not `unavailable`.

readings.description: Every position that read the line, as an unordered bag. Two entries that print alike are two readings.

axis.description: The position this reading met the line at, as `boundaries[].axis` names it.

against.description: What a row at this reading has to do, in this position's terms — `boundaries[].items[].against` for the same border and point.

where.description: What every row at this reading has to be beside the values: which cases of a sum a value is or is not, whether it holds a value, which truth it is, as the cases the line decides in hold them, less what the position read already names. Absent where those cases hold no value of the input to a case or a truth; the relations they ask beside it are not said here.

hit.description: Whether some row stands at the point as read here.

items.description: One position that read the line, and what a row there has to do in that position's terms. A bag and not a set: two readings that print alike are two readings — what tells them apart is where the line was met, which this document does not carry — so a consumer may count these but may not deduplicate them. The order is not a contract.

axis.description: What the line is on, in the words the declaration wrote — `String.length(value)`. Present exactly where the obligation is one a declaration owns: a line a body's rule drew has no such word, since each reading names the position it met the line at and none can stand for the rest.

against.description: What a row here has to do, on `axis`. Present exactly with it.

allOf.description: What the line is on and what a row has to do on it are the author's words, and only a line a declaration drew has them.
Whether some row stands at the point is written exactly where the measurement has a value.
Why there is no answer is written exactly where there is none.
A ground is named exactly where one was established.
And none where none was.

declaredLine.description: Which line of one conjunct of a declaration's clause a line is. Two shapes, because a conjunct draws lines two ways and neither is the other: a comparison inside it places an end of its own, and the conjunct can leave the values somewhere none of its comparisons places — which is found by asking what the rules leave without that conjunct, and is the conjunct's line rather than any statement's. The numbers here count the statements of the one conjunct named beside this, so they mean nothing away from it.

oneOf.description: The line one statement of the conjunct placed. `statement` is which of that conjunct's statements it is, counted from zero over everything the conjunct states rather than over the comparisons among them — a choice states neither of its sides and holds its place.

The line the conjunct draws, which no statement of it places. `pairedWith` is which of the conjunct's statements are about the number this line is on, and it is what tells this line from the line the same conjunct draws on another number. None of them drew it: what was taken away is the conjunct, and it takes away everything the conjunct states — so a document naming one of them would be saying that statement placed an end which another statement of the same conjunct is why.

whichLine.description: Which of a rule's lines a line is, said by what named it. The three kinds of rule are not decomposed alike, and no two of their numbers mean the same thing: a declaration's clause is written in the parts its author joined and each of those draws lines of its own, so a line of one is named by the part and by which of that part's lines it is; a part of a behavior's clause states as many things as a reading of it finds, so a line of one is named by the part and by which of that part's statements it is; a comparison written in a body is a rule apiece, so a line of one is named by the rule alone — or, where it states several relations held together, by the rule and which of its lines it is. Written as one number, a consumer was handed a count without being told which of the three made it. The rule stands inside this rather than beside it so that only the pairs this compiler can build are documents: there is no shape here that gives a body's comparison a part, or a declaration's clause a statement of a behavior's.

oneOf.description: A line of a declaration's clause. `part` is where the conjunct it came out of stands among the parts of that clause, counted from zero, and it means something only beside the rule — two clauses each have a part numbered nought. One part draws more than one line, so `line` says which of them this is: a denial is carried to the leaves as a clause is read, so a conjunct written as a denied choice states one comparison per branch and places an end on each of the numbers they are about. Named by the part alone, those are one line — and the facts beside them do not tell them apart, since two lower bounds admitting their own value say the same thing about two numbers.

One statement of one part of a behavior's clause. Both are written because they are counted in different things: the parts are counted over the clause and the statements over one part, so the second statement of the second part is the fourth of nothing. `statement` counts everything the part states and not the comparisons among them — a choice states neither of its sides and holds its place — so a consumer that counted the comparisons it could see would land elsewhere.

A comparison written in a body, which is a rule apiece: a condition holding three of them is three rules, each with a line of its own. Where its definition writes no choice on the way to it, the comparison is one line, read wherever a call puts it: two calls of a helper read it at two places, and a row at either is a row at the line the author wrote.

One of the lines a comparison written in a body draws, where its definition writes a choice on the way to it: `Int.max(a, b) > 5` is one rule with a line under each arm of `max`, and a row at one says nothing about the other. `arms` is which of them this is: the arm taken at each choice the comparison's definition writes, outermost first, in the source's coordinates. What a caller hands the definition is no part of it, so every call of a helper reads the same lines, each at the places that call puts it. Each line is owed rows only where the statement turns on it.

writtenArm.description: One arm the author of a comparison took on the way to one of its lines. `construct` is the choice the source wrote — an `if`, a `match`, or an operation applied whose answer is one of its arguments — and `through` the calls and references the comparison's definition makes to reach it, outermost first; a choice reached through a function a caller handed in is no arm of the comparison's and is not written here. `arm` is which arm, numbered from zero in the order the source writes them, and `selects` says the line is drawn by what selects that arm rather than by what the arm answers.

items.description: A call by where it is written (`at`), or a name written where a value goes by which reference of which definition it is.

writtenConstruct.description: A construct a source wrote: the module, the definition where a body wrote it, the number the definition counted its constructs by, and which fork a lowering made of it. Not a place in a source, which `sources` answers for.

ruleId.description: What tells one rule of the model from every other, which is not what a reader is shown. The coordinates differ by kind because rules are told apart by different things, and every part of an identity is written: a declaration is its module and its name — two modules may each declare an `Amount`, and they are two types — and a comparison is the construct a definition wrote, numbered from zero within that definition, so which definition is part of which construct. A document written before the numbering was counted within a definition carries no `definition` and numbers over the whole source instead, which is what its absence says. A predicate carries one where a definition's body wrote it and says so in `writtenIn`, since a behavior writes such a rule in its body and in its own clauses alike; the remaining kinds never carry one. Each kind names the coordinates it carries and takes no others, which is why none of them lists what it may not have: a coordinate a later version adds for one kind is refused by the rest for not having been named there, rather than by somebody remembering to forbid it in each. A key within this document rather than a name; a consumer groups by it and shows `rule`. It names the rule and not the question — one rule raises more than one, and `question` and `subject` beside it are what tell those apart.

kind.description: Which kind of rule of the model this is, and so which coordinates below are written. A `predicate` is a rule a body writes as one of the language's own operations over the values at a position — `String.startsWith("JP", code)` — which tells a set of them from the rest and draws no line; a behavior states one in its body and in its own `ensures` alike, and it is identified by the application the author wrote together with what wrote it, which `writtenIn` says. A rule of a body is a comparison and not the construct it is written in: it may stand in the condition of an `if` or a `guard`, be given a name above the fork that tests it, or be what the behavior answers with, and it is one rule in all of those. Documents of version 3 wrote `guard` here, from the days when a rule was found by finding a fork. A `fork` is the other way round and is not that word come back: it is a fork whose condition states none of the kinds above, so what the model divides on there is something this compiler did not read, and the fork itself is what a question about it is filed under.

declaredIn.description: The module the rule is written in. Part of every identity here: names are unique within a module and not across them, and a construct's number starts again in each definition.

declaredOn.description: The declaration an invariant's clause is written on.

behavior.description: The behavior an `ensures` clause reads, or the one whose answer a body's comparison or predicate is read for. For a comparison this is not where it is written: a helper's comparison is read by every behavior that calls it, and `definition` says which definition wrote it. The same holds for a predicate `writtenIn` says a body wrote; for one its own clauses wrote, this is the behavior that wrote it as well, which is why the name is written once.

definition.description: The definition whose source wrote the construct, present in a document whose `ordinal` is counted within one. For a comparison, a document written before construct numbering became a count within a definition has none, and its `ordinal` is a count over the whole source instead — so which of the two a number means is read from whether this is here. For a predicate, what counted the ordinal is said by `writtenIn`, and this is written exactly where that is `body`.

writtenIn.description: What wrote the application a predicate is, which is what its `ordinal` was counted within. A behavior states such a rule in a definition's body and in its own `ensures`, the constructs of the two are numbered apart, and both start at zero — so without this the first of each is one identity. `body` writes `definition` beside it; `stated` is the behavior's own statement of itself, which `behavior` already names.

clause.description: Where the clause sits among the ones written beside it, counted from zero.

arm.description: Where the rule sits among the arms of its `ensures` clause, counted from zero. Two arms may name one case and are two rules.

ordinal.description: The construct the rule was written as, counted from zero among the constructs written by whatever counted it. For a comparison that is `definition`, and where `definition` is absent the document is an earlier one and this counts the constructs of the whole source. For a predicate it is what `writtenIn` names: the definition `definition` names, or the behavior's own statement of itself, whose name is `behavior`.

lowered.description: Which of the comparisons one written construct lowered to this is, for a construct that lowers to more than one.

coverageQuestion.description: What a rule of the model leaves that something has to answer. `admitted_values` is which values may stand at a position, and `boundary` is a border rows are owed at. The other two are rules this compiler did not read far enough to classify, and they are not one word because they are not one state: `boundaryNotDetermined` is a rule read far enough to say it restricts the values where it was filed and not far enough to say whether it also puts an end there — the classes are settled and only the border measure waits on it — while `notDetermined` is a rule nothing worked out at all, which holds both measures. `regionNotDetermined` is a rule whose classes at the position were shown over some of its values, where which class the rest are in nothing worked out: the classes stand and the partition measure waits on the rest, while the border measure does not. None of the three names a subject, since working one out is part of what did not happen, and the `stopped` beside either says what would have to be read further. Those four are what this compiler issues, and a word arrives here in the same change that starts raising it. `singleton` and `partition` are retired: a comparison this compiler reads owes the row at the value it singles out and the rows in the classes its line makes, and it owes them by having been read — so they are carried as the partition's own geometry rather than as questions standing against an answer. They are kept because reports of this version carried them, and a reader of an older document still meets them.

status.description: Whether a measure has a number. `unavailable` says only that it has none; the `reason` beside it says why, and the two are not read off one another.

measureReason.description: Where a measure writes the reason beside its status: at `unavailable` and nowhere else. Said once and referred to by every measure rather than written into each of them, because it is one relation — spelled at each, it would be a relation wherever somebody wrote it again and prose wherever they did not, which is what it was. A measure with a number has nothing here to say: what stopped it is a question about a measure that stopped.

declarations.description: What each of the module's own declarations is owed and is short of. A line an `invariant` drew is a fact about the type wherever the type is carried, so it is owed once and is not any behavior's: published under one of them it would be published under whichever a walk reached first. Grouped by who owes it, since a line two declarations took an end in together is owed to both.

lines.description: Every line these declarations drew that some behavior of the module reads, once each however many positions carry the type — what the human-readable report counts as the declarations' `borders`. What a row is owed at on one is under `obligations` and what no row is owed at is under `excluded`, each filed by whose the point is, which need not be the declarations that drew the line.

lineId.description: Which line, by the two parts an `obligationId` names a line by.

label.description: Where the line is, in the words the declaration wrote for what it is on. A rendering and never a key.

noPoint.description: The roles the line has no point in, which its own rule settles: `the_class_at_the_line_holds_one_value` is a rule naming one value, which puts that value in a class of its own and leaves no row in it away from the line. Empty where the line has a point in every role.

excluded.description: The points no row is owed at that are these declarations' fact, once each however many positions carry the type. Filed by whose the point is, as `obligations` are: a point a type's bound leaves out on its own is the type's, and the same role of the same bound where a record's clause on the field empties the region beside it is another point, told apart by `stops` and filed under whose it is — the declarations whose line it is, and a declaration that took in the end the region stops at. A fact the declarations settled and not an obligation: none of these is in `obligations`, and none is a row anybody is short of.

pointId.description: Which point: the line and its level and where on the quantity, which an `obligationId` names a point by, and where else it was settled. Two entries that differ only in `stops` are two points — the run above a type's bound holds values where nothing else stops it, and is empty where a record's clause holds the field at the bound.

stops.description: Where else it was settled, each written as an obligation's `stops` is: the far end of the empty run beside the line, or an end the rules leave the position at that refuses the value. Empty where the line alone settled it. A set: the order carries no meaning.

point.description: Which of the four coverage items this point is. Not what tells two of them apart: two points of one line can carry one of these words, and `pointId` is what they differ by.

label.description: Where the line is, in the words the declaration wrote for what it is on, and the level where the line states one on that quantity. A rendering and never a key.

notOwed.description: Why no row is owed at the point, in the words a behavior's `boundaries` item uses for the same answer.

name.description: What a report calls the owners above. A rendering and never a key: two sets of declarations a report writes alike are two sets.

obligations.description: What these declarations' lines are owed, once each however many positions carry the type — the declarations' side of the same relation a behavior's `partition.obligations` is the body's side of, and where a finding of kind `boundary_unmet` or `domain_point_uncovered` about one of them joins. Every one of them and not only what the module is short of: a line a row already stands at raises no finding, so a section written from the findings alone could not tell a module whose declarations owe nothing from one whose every line is answered. Each carries `axis`, the words the declaration wrote for what its line is on.

owners.description: Which of the module's declarations owe the lines below, in their own order. A list, because a line two declarations took an end in together is owed to both and is one entry here — `name` beside it is how a report says such a pair and is not the name of a declaration. Ordered by the declarations themselves and not by which reading of the line was met first, so the entry a reader finds them under does not turn on a walk.

implementation.description: Where the body comes from. `injected` is Java's to supply; `unimplemented` is Souther's to write and not written. Neither has a body here, so the rows of either are recorded rather than evaluated.

rows.description: How many example rows name this behavior, across every source that writes one. Written where this behavior's rows were read and absent where they were not, which is a fact about the reading and is in no field of this object — so the absence is the answer rather than something a reader works out from what is beside it: a source nobody could evaluate leaves no row to count, and a build that reads no rows counted none of them. So `0` is a behavior whose rows were read and numbered none, which is what an author acts on differently from rows nobody looked at — the two were one number until this version, and a model being migrated onto read as one with no rows written. Which of the ways it was is `status` and `weakening` beside it.

pending.description: How many of those rows are recorded rather than evaluated. Present and absent exactly where `rows` is, and for the same reason.

rowsThatDoNotHold.description: The rows written for this behavior that ran, or were to run, and did not do what they say, in the order they were read — each with where it stopped. Empty where none, and never absent. Not part of `adequacy`: whether the rows cover what the model owes and whether they hold are two questions, and a row that does not hold is evidence of what it reached before it stopped all the same. Each is keyed as its entry of `rowObligations` is.

rowObligations.description: Every row written for this behavior and whether the answer it owes is written. Not `rows` said again: that count is of the rows a reading handed back and is absent where nothing ran, while this is read off the text — so a behavior can have every one of its rows here and no count beside them, which says the rows were written and no observation came back. How many are waiting is a fold of this array and is written nowhere else. A row whose answer no parse could read is not here: it is malformed, a diagnostic says how, and counting it would put a source full of syntax errors in front of a reader as work an author had left.

disposition.description: Where the row stands. `met` is a row that states what it expects; `unmet` is a row written `<?>`, which a build refuses over and which an `unanswered_row` finding keyed on this row joins to. An `unanswered_row` finding keyed on an arm is about the arm and joins `branch.obligations` instead. There is no third: whether a row's answer is owed is a fact about the text, settled where the row was read and true whatever became of the evaluation.

reachProofsContradicted.description: The proofs this compiler made that nothing arrives somewhere in this body, that a row then went against: an arm proven to be gone into by nothing that a row went through, a comparison proven to come out one way for nothing that a row brought out so, a comparison or an application whose answer states a line proven to be arrived at by nothing that a row came to, a way through the decision proven to be taken by no input that a row went down. Nothing about the model is wrong then and the proof is, and every measure here reads the body with it taken back. Of the reading and of no measure: which measures rested on one says so in its own words — `denominatorSettled` and `proof_contradicted` for the arms, `reachProofsContradicted` on a rule of the decision for one the proof would have left no row — and a proof no measure rested on is listed here all the same. Each proof once, however many rules rested on it. Only a place a run is recorded at can be shown wrong here: an arm that answers `unreachable` has no such place, and a row reaching one is E1911, not an entry of this list. Nor is an author's `unreachable` claim judged again here — that is the compile's, read from the model before any row ran. Absent where no row went against any.

walkProofsContradicted.description: The walks this compiler proved go over one element at most, that a row then took a second element of: a fold whose list the model's rules and the conditions on the way leave one element at most, and a run that went past its first. Nothing about the model is wrong then and the proof is, and the rewrites of the walk are asked as if it had not been made. Beside `reachProofsContradicted` and not among its entries, since that list is of proofs that nothing arrives somewhere and this is a proof about how long a list is. Each walk once, named the way a rewrite of it is in an obligation identity, however many places it is entered at. Absent where no row went against any.

reachProof.description: One place a proof that nothing arrives was about, as it stands in the tree that runs: `construct` is the copy of the construct, in the coordinates a combination's decision is written under, so a helper called twice is two copies and what one call cannot reach another may. `arm` is an arm of a fork, by `part`, its place among the fork's arms; `comparison_outcome` a comparison coming out one way, `held` saying which; `arrival` a construct a line is drawn at — a comparison, or an application whose answer states one — proven to be arrived at by nothing as a whole, which is not either way out of a comparison, since both may be rightly proven while this is wrong. `way_no_input_takes` is a way through the body's decision that its reading proved no input takes, written under `way` as a rule of the decision is identified, by the conditions the way consulted; it carries no `construct`, since a way is the conditions of several, and no rule of the decision rests on it, since none past it was read.

findings.description: Everything the measures found about one subject and nothing filled, and what a build does about each. The measures above each say what they measured; this says which findings came out of them and which of those a build refuses over, which no measure's own object can say.

allOf.description: The code is written for the kinds a build is told about and for no others. A kind that carries one carries it wherever it is written, since which code a finding is told under is the kind's and not this finding's.

And the place is written for the kinds whose place is their own: an arm is shown at the fork it is one of, a row waiting for its answer at the row or at the arm it stands at, and an arm rewritten as its sibling at the fork the two are arms of. A fold rewritten is shown at the fold where the build holds the source it is written in, and at the declaration the entry already names where it does not, so its place may or may not be written. The rest are cited at the declaration the entry already names, and a place written for them would be that declaration's said twice — which is where a body rewritten as one answer is shown.
Which thing a row is owed for is written exactly for the kinds that are about one, and its shape is the shape that account keeps.

then.description: One of two, because one kind covers two obligations: the arm a row stands at is owed a row and the arm account holds that, and the row itself is owed an answer and the row account holds that. Which of them a finding is about is what it publishes here.
A whole line held against one line of its fault family, and not one of its points: what is owed here is that the rows rule that line out, and no point of it is the thing that is owed.
A rewrite of the body, and not a place in it: what is owed is a row the rewrite answers differently on, wherever that row stands.

A position of a computation of a value derived from several positions, cut at several places, and not a point of any border: what is owed is rows beside the borders of the computation that fail a computation weighing the position one more and one weighing it one less, which is what fixes how it weighs into the value.

kind.description: What the measure established. `output_case_unspecified` is a case of the output no row expects and `output_case_unverified` is one some row expects and nothing was seen to produce; `input_case_unspecified` is a case of an input no row applies the behavior to and `axis_class_uncovered` is a class of a derived position no row is in — the two read alike about one class and only one of them is refused over. `boundary_unmet` is a line some rule draws that no row sits on, `arm_unreached` an arm of the body no row goes through. `boundary_not_told_from_another` is a line every point of which a row does sit on, and which the rows still do not tell from a line weighing one of its positions one more or one less: rows at a border's points show a line that has not moved, and showing one of the lines beside it wrong takes a row that line answers differently at. The lines it is held against are the ones one step away, so a border nothing is said about has no one-step fault left in it, which is a fault domain stated rather than the geometry of the line pinned down.
