Its `subject` names both lines, the one the rule drew and the one the rows leave standing beside it. `tilt_of_a_derived_value_not_shown` is a position of a value a computation derives from several positions and cuts at several places, as a table of thresholds cuts the value it is looked up by, whose weight no rows fix: no row beside the borders of the computation fails a computation weighing the position one more, or none fails one weighing it one less. It is owed once for the computation and once for each position, and never once for each threshold, and it stands where the positions' own classes would otherwise have been divided by the value's thresholds. Its `subject` names the value and the position. `unanswered_row` is a row written with its answer still owed, and an arm whose only rows are those — told apart from `arm_unreached` because a row does go through such an arm, and read off the source rather than measured, so nothing about how much of the model could be read takes it away. `partition_not_derivable`, `partition_not_read` and `partition_rules_not_reached` are positions the model divides no way, what a reading did not read, and positions the axes did measure whose rules the walk never reached. `partition_values_not_separated` is none of those: every rule about the position arrived and every one was read, and what the reading holds is one set per position standing for a relation two of them cannot state — so the values it reports may be wider than the declarations leave the position, and a class made out of them may be one no value can be in. It carries no `reason` and no `ruleId`, because no rule is answerable for it and what would lift it is a reading that keeps the alternatives apart. A `partition_not_read` is one of two things and `ruleId` says which: with it, a rule this read and could not turn into a line, named because the reader that stopped knows which rule; without it, a position whose rules the reading never arrived at, where no rule is named because none was seen. `reason` is on both, and says which limit is in the way. `rule_unaccounted` is one question a rule raised that nothing answered — said whether or not an axis came back for the position it is about, since a rule this compiler could not read is exactly the one no axis is derived from, and named for the question rather than for a measure because which section a reader meets it under follows from what it asks. `rewrite_unnoticed` is a rewrite of the body — an arm rows go through answering as a sibling of it, a fold rows enter stopping after its first element or handing every step the seed, or the body answering one value the rows observed — that some input is shown to be answered differently by and under which no row comes out differently. Reaching an arm shows it ran and not that anything a row states depends on it, so this is said of what the rows do reach. `rule_may_stop_a_run` is a rule a run reaching it may stop in — an operation it is read through ends the run on one of the ways it is worked out, such as a division by nought — where the ways before it are not shown to leave no row for the stop. A possibility and not a run shown to exist: a stop is dropped only where the conditions on the way are shown to rule it out. It is said of the rule whatever line it draws, or none, names the rule by `ruleId`, and carries no `reason`, because nothing was left unread. A rule every run stops in draws no line and is a `partition_not_read` entry with the reason `rule_answers_nowhere`.

disposition.description: What a build does about this one. `refused` is an obligation shown unmet, which `--strict` and a warned build refuse over; `reported` is a finding about no obligation — what was seen rather than what is owed — whatever its measurement managed; `undecided` is an obligation from a measurement that came to no answer, so nothing is shown about it — telling an author to write a row they may already have written is worse than saying nothing, so it is named and not refused.

obligationId.description: Which thing a row is owed for the finding is about, written exactly where the finding is about one — which is also where `disposition` says a build acts on it, since the two are one fact about the finding's subject written in two fields. What a consumer joins the finding to its obligation by — in `partition.obligations` where a body's rule drew the line, in `declarations[].obligations` where one of the module's declarations owns it, in `branch.obligations` where it is an arm of the body, in `rowObligations` where it is a row waiting on its answer, in `signature.output.obligations` where it is a case of the output, and in `partition.axes` where it is a class of a position. Its shape is the shape the account it is an entry of keeps, and the shape is what says which account that is — a point of a line, an arm, an axis and a class, a row, a case of an output, and the rest are distinct and closed, so a consumer reads the key and knows where to look it up. Not settled by `kind`: that word is a coarser sort than what a finding is about, and more than one of them covers subjects owed at different accounts. `unanswered_row` is the plain case — a row waiting for its answer is owed at the row, and the arm it stands at is owed a row of its own, and the two are told apart here and nowhere else. `input_case_unspecified` is the same shape of thing: a case of an input is one obligation with the class of its position only where the behavior has a position of its own, so it is an axis and a class where it does, and the behavior, the input's number and the case where its input is read at its stages and nothing divides it. `subject` beside it is what a reader is shown, and two obligations are shown the same words where what differs is not in the words: one rule at one level in one role owes two `in` points when two cases stop the run in different places, a fork whose caller supplies the rule owes one arm per rule handed in at one place and under one label, and two positions of one behavior divide into classes that read alike. A combination of a body's decisions is one of these too, written as the decisions a run has to have made. A whole line held against one line of its fault family is the one shape with no place in it: it is owed at `partition.boundaries[].besides` rather than at a point of the line, and a place would name a point the obligation is not about.

ruleId.description: Which rule the finding is about, where it is about one. `subject` beside it is what a reader is shown, and two rules an author named alike are shown the same words — so this is what says they are two. It names the rule and not the question: one rule raises more than one, and `subject` beside it is what tells those apart. Written for `rule_unaccounted`, and for `partition_not_read` where that entry is about a rule rather than about a position the reading never arrived at — which is why it is required for the first and only allowed for the second. It is also required for `rule_may_stop_a_run`. The other kinds are not about a rule and never carry it.

reason.description: Which limit stopped the reading, present exactly on `partition_not_read`. The same word the `partition.notRead` entry this came from carries, and what a consumer joins the two by. Written because a rule can be stopped at one position by two limits at once — one conjunct of a clause relating two positions and the conjunct beside it in a form nothing reads — and the findings are then two, differing here and nowhere else.

subject.description: What the finding is about, written to name what is already in this document: a class name is one of an axis's `classes`, an arm's label one in `branch.obligations`, `axis = value` names the point of a declaration's line the way the declaration wrote it, and `ON point of comparison@billing.sou:14:22` says which of the four points a boundary finding is about and which rule drew the line — the rule as a `ruleHandle`, and a line a body drew is owed once wherever it is read and has no one quantity to be named by, so what a row there has to do is under the obligation's `readings`. A finding about a question nothing answered leads with the same handle and says what was asked after it. These words are a presentation and never a key: which obligation such a finding is about is `obligationId`. An input's case carries its position — `C (in #1)` — because two parameters of one type give two findings a class name alone cannot tell apart.

pattern.description: Which set of choices the finding is about, present exactly on `interaction_uncovered`: the group, and the outcome it takes at each factor. Joins to the entry of `interaction.groups` that has the same `group`, and to the member of its `unobserved` that has the same `fixed`. Not an `obligationId`: a set of choices is not an obligation of the body, and the decisions two sets share say nothing of whether they are one set.

combinations.description: How many choices of the group the finding is about, present exactly on `interaction_uncovered`. A finding is about the choices of one group that no row makes and that stand alike in what the reading went without and what is open about them; a combination that two groups arrive at is counted in each.

code.description: The code a build is told this under, present exactly where the kind has one. A kind a build is never told about carries no code rather than an empty one.

everyRunStops.description: On `rule_may_stop_a_run` only, where it is known: the rows at which every run that gets to the rule stops in one operation the rule is read through, because what the operation works out is past what its type holds and every operation a run may work out before it is within its own. Said only where every operation that can stop a run there is known, and not of rows at which two operations that may come in either order are both past their types. A proof about those rows and not a class of them: the rule is neither true nor false there, no row there is a witness for either side, and nothing is left open, so no measure waits on it. Absent where no such row is known.

operation.description: The operation every run there stops in, as the numbers it is over weighed and a constant.

where.description: The rows, as forms over the numbers of the input each between two ends: every row meeting all of them stops in the operation. A form over one number is that number's run; a form over several says what one number alone does not, as where two together pass the type. An end a type already holds every row to is not written.

form.description: The numbers weighed, as an author would write them.

least.description: The least value the form takes there; absent where only the type bounds it below.

greatest.description: The greatest value the form takes there; absent where only the type bounds it above.

at.description: Where the finding is, present exactly where its place is its own rather than the declaration it sits under — `arm_unreached` and nothing else. A behavior with two `guard`s has two arms labelled `else`, so the place is what tells two of these apart, and it is the same place under the same key as the matching `branch.obligations` entry, whose `disposition` is `unmet`. The other kinds are cited at the behavior's own declaration, which the entry above already names.

ruleObligationId.description: What tells one rule of a body's decision from every other, which is not what a reader is shown. The behavior and what the path consulted, each condition written as the proposition an account keys on: a comparison and its denial are one column, so `n > 100` in a source is written here as `n <= 100` denied. That is what makes the table exclusive and it is why none of it goes into a sentence — `subject` beside it says only which behavior, and the notes point at the construct the author wrote. A condition the path never consulted is absent, which is what a rule leaving it out means. `conditions` is sorted by what each is written as and not by the order a walk met them: two runs that read one body's ways in two orders state one rule.

behavior.description: Whose decision it is a rule of. Rules are written in the terms of a body's own positions, so two behaviors comparing same-named positions the same way state equal rules.

conditions.description: One entry per condition the path consulted.

kind.description: Which distinction the column is, over whatever the body decided on: a position of the input, or what a dependency answered — the two are written the same way and `condition` says which. `comparison` is a comparison the arithmetic took in, `truth` a value read for whether it holds, `case` a fork read as the case the subject turned out to be, `statement` a condition read to the end that is none of those — some element meeting something, several things asked at once, an arm a computed value decides — written as what it states, and `not_read` a condition this compiler has no words for — told apart by the occurrence that met it, because two conditions nothing could read mean nothing to be told apart by.

condition.description: Which distinction, as the account keys it.

outcome.description: What the path came out as: `held` or `denied` for a comparison, a truth and a condition nothing read, and the case the subject was read as for a fork.

notRead.description: Why a condition nothing read was not, every reason once — written only for `not_read`, beside the identity and no part of it. `meaning_unread` is what the condition means not having been read, `outside_domain` the domain the reader writes in having no words for what it means, and `past_a_figure` the reader having the words and stopping at a figure of this compiler's work before saying it in them. A condition read to the end and in the reader's words is taken, whether or not anything composes a row for it, so neither is written for what composing reaches.

conditionNotReadReason.description: One reason a condition nothing read was not: which of the three kinds, and the word within it. The kinds are told apart by what lifts one — a rule of the reading of what a condition means, a wider domain, or a higher figure. `more_ways_than_are_read` is some or every element meeting the condition coming, taken apart, to more ways an element may meet it than a reading of one condition makes; `more_alternatives_than_are_tried` is a condition that is one of several things, whose parts a path takes alone to know which of them it leaves, coming — counted inside one another — to more parts than a reading of one condition takes alone; `more_choices_than_are_written_out` is a condition counting how many of some statements hold, taken apart into the choices of which of them hold, coming written out to more parts than a reader of them is handed. For none of them is anything about the model or about either domain short. Each `outside_domain` word names the reader whose domain stops: what a row is asked is written at the input's positions, so `answer_a_row_stands_in` is what a dependency answered and `node_below_what_a_row_writes` is a node a search reaches further down than a row is written; what a path knows is relations of numbers, truths and what every element was written to meet, about the places of the tree it walks, so the `path_` words and `place_the_path_does_not_read` are where that stops. `size_nothing_measures` and `position_the_reading_holds_no_place_for` are no longer written — every container a condition asks about has a size that is a number of the input, and the reading of the input holds every position a condition names — and a document of this version may still carry them.

reason.description: The word for the reason within its kind.

replacementObligationId.description: What tells one rewrite of a body from every other: the behavior and which rewrite. `arm_as_sibling` is an arm answering as another arm of the same fork, written with the fork's coordinates the way an arm is, `part` the arm rewritten and `with` the sibling it answers as. `fold_after_one_step` is a fold stopping after its first element, and `fold_from_the_seed` a fold whose every step is handed the seed in place of what the step before it answered, both written with the coordinates of the fold the source wrote the way a fork's are; a fold written inside one of the language's own operations is written with that operation's coordinates. `one_answer` is the body answering one value the rows observed whatever it is given, one rewrite per value, and `answeredBy` is the first row that answered that value — the value named by a row that came to it, in the words a row is named by elsewhere in this document, rather than written out in a form of its own. A key within this document: it names an entry of `replacement.obligations`, and a consumer joins a `rewrite_unnoticed` finding to the rewrite it is about on it.

answeredBy.description: The row a body answering one value is named by: its source, and its name where it wrote one and its ordinal within the source where it did not.

replacement.description: The rewrites of this behavior's body and whether a row tells each from the body as written. Beside `branch` and not among it: a row goes through an arm whatever the arm answers, so every arm can be reached by rows none of which would fail if it answered as its sibling, and a fold can be entered by rows none of which runs its step on what an earlier step answered. One entry per rewrite put to the rows, whatever they came to — a `rewrite_unnoticed` finding names one of these by its `obligationId`. Absent where the compile did not get far enough for the rewrites to be asked about.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. `no_body` is a behavior with no body of its own to rewrite, which no row would change. `not_asked` is a build that did not ask for the rows to be run again under a rewrite, and `no_rows` a behavior no row names. `body_was_not_read` is the model saying a body is written here and the image this run was measured in not carrying it, and `unreadable` is rows that ran without the classes a rewrite is carried in.

disposition.description: What the rows came to about this rewrite. `noticed` is a row that comes out the other way under the rewrite: it holds of one of the two bodies and fails of the other. `unnoticed` is a rewrite some input is shown to be answered differently by, under which no row comes out differently. `undecided` is neither shown: no such input was found, or the rewrite could not be put to the rows, and nothing here concludes the rewrite answers as the body does.

undecidedBecause.description: Every way a rewrite was left open, in the order the words are listed here, each said as itself: a search stopped by two figures was stopped by both, and a reader raising one is owed the other. `too_large` is a fork that carrying the sibling would grow past what a class may hold, or a fold whose switch the method it is written in could not hold. `a_statement_was_not_read` is a row stating something this could not read, or one that neither held nor failed of the body as written. `no_row_answered_differently` is a search that composed rows and found the rewrite answering each as the body does — where it looked, and not everywhere. `runs_spent` is a search that made as many runs as the measure lets one rewrite take with rows left; `a_composing_figure_reached` one whose composing stopped at a figure of its own; `a_run_did_not_come_back` one where a run it asked for came back with no answer it could read. `nothing_was_composed` is a search that composed no row to look at, and `nothing_ran` is nothing able to run a row. `step_not_expanded` is retired: it was a fold whose step is chosen as the program runs, or reaches the fold as a value, which a build before it could not run rewritten. A report written then carries it, and no build raises it now.

combinationObligationId.description: What tells one combination of a body's decisions from every other: the behavior, and the decisions a run has to have made. Not what a reader is shown — the decisions are held in the terms the account keys on, and `subject` beside a finding says only which behavior. `decisions` is sorted by what each is written as here and not by the order a walk met them: what a run has to have done is a set, so two documents of one model write it the same way round.

items.description: One decision of the body coming out one way. `case` is a union the body matched on, named by the position and the case. `comparison` is a comparison of the body, named by the construct and which way it came out — the number it compares is not part of it, because the construct is what tells one decision from another. `arm` is a fork the reading could not name a position for, named by the fork and which arm.

outcome.description: Which case, for a case; `held` or `denied` for a comparison.

visit.description: Which time a run evaluates the comparison, counted from zero, written only for a comparison a run evaluates more than once and absent otherwise. A comparison in a closure applied to each element of a list written in the body is one construct and as many decisions as there are elements, so two combinations that differ in which element came out which way name the same construct and the same outcomes; this is what tells them apart.

part.description: Which arm of the fork, for an arm.

copySite.description: Where a copy was made, said by exactly one of three: a call by where it is written (`module`, `definition`, `call`, `lowered`, all four); a name written where a value goes by `name`; a block handed over and applied by `supplied`. Applied to the object that carries the fields.

namedReference.description: A name written where a value goes, which a copy of what it names was made at: which reference of which definition of which module it is.

suppliedBlock.description: A block handed to a parameter and applied, which a copy of it was made at: the copy it was handed to (`handedTo`, what was copied and where that copy was made), the parameter of that copy it filled, and where it was applied (`appliedAt`, a call or a name). Two applications of one block and two blocks applied at one place are told apart here.

materialisationRegion.description: The region one build of a value was made for, said as the source settles it. `kind` says how: `body` is a definition's body as a whole; `slot` is one of the regions a construct the source wrote opens, named by the construct and `slot`; `block` is the body of a block the source wrote, by its `rule` number; `block_of_name` is the body of a block a name written where a value goes was expanded into, by which reference of that definition the name is; `invariant` is one clause of a type's invariant as a whole, by the `declaration` that writes it and the clause's `ordinal`; `ensures` is one arm of a behavior's ensures clause as a whole, by the behavior (`definition`), the clause's `ordinal` and the `arm`. Every arm carries what tells one of its regions from every other, and none of another arm's: a document naming a region two ways is a document a join could pick either of.

declaration.description: The type whose invariant a build was made for, by the name it is declared under.

ordinal.description: Which clause of that invariant, or of that behavior's ensures, counted from zero in the order the clauses are written.

arm.description: Which arm of that ensures clause, counted from zero in the order the arms are written.

clause.description: The invariant clause a refused arm answers for; absent for the arm that answers for any.

cases.description: The case names a `match` arm was written for.

index.description: Which of a comprehension's guards, in the order they were written.

reference.description: Which reference of the definition the name written where a value goes is.

pairCellObligationId.description: What tells one combination of two of a behavior's classes from every other, where the pair space is the criterion it is held to: the behavior and the two classes, each named by its position. A class id is unique within its axis and not across two, so a pair of ids without their positions is one two combinations answer to. Sorted by position and class, because a combination is a pair and not an order of them.

inputCaseObligationId.description: What tells one case of one input from every other, where nothing divides that input into classes. A behavior whose input is read at its stages has no position of its own for a class to be of, so the case is what the account keys on: the behavior, which of its inputs by number, and which case. The number and not a name, because such a behavior declares no parameters to name one by — and a stage's parameter name is that stage's, whose own classes are entries of `partition.axes` under its own axis. A row of a stage discharges the stage's obligation and a row of this behavior discharges this one, so the two are not joined by anything here.

behavior.description: The behavior whose input it is.

input.description: Which of its inputs, in the order the signature takes them.

case.description: The case of that input, as the model declares it.

borderObligationId.description: What tells one line a rule draws, held against one line of its fault family, from every other such obligation, where what is owed is of the whole line rather than of a point on it. The line, the level it is read at, and the line of the family, and no place: a point of the line is somewhere, and a line held against a line beside it is nowhere in particular — what would answer it is an input that rules the other line out, which is not a point this line owns. A key within this document: it names an entry of `besides` under a `partition.boundaries` entry, and a consumer joins a `boundary_not_told_from_another` finding to the line it is about on it. A comparison written in a body carries no level: the value each call puts it at is the reading's, and the line is the one its author wrote.

direction.description: The line of the family, spelled as an author writes a form and with no threshold: where the rows leave the threshold moves with every row written, and the obligation does not. One obligation per line of the family, because a row ruling one of them out need not rule out another.

constructOccurrence.description: Which construct of which body, and which copy of it. The same coordinates an arm is written under, so a consumer joining a decision to the arm it goes through joins on these. `construct` is the number the body counted its constructs by and `lowered` which fork a lowering made of it — neither is a place in a source, which `sources` answers for.

items.description: One step the copy was made by, and `kind` says which. An `expansion` is a copy of what `expanded` names, made at one site: a call, by where it is written (`module`, `definition`, `call`, `lowered`); a name written where a value goes, by `name`; or a block handed to a parameter and applied, by `supplied`. Exactly one of the three. A `materialisation` is one build of a value's body, for the region `at` names.

through.description: The calls and builds the copy was made through, in the order they were made. Absent where the construct is where it was written: a helper spliced into two calls holds one construct twice under one `construct` number, and a value built for two regions holds its constructs twice under the same calls; this is what tells the copies apart. A key within one compilation and no name to match two documents by, because which builds there are follows how the compiler shares them.

tiltObligationId.description: What tells the weight of one position in a value a computation derives from several positions from every other thing a row is owed for. The computation — the comparison the author wrote and the copy of it a call of a helper made — and the position, and never a threshold: the value is computed once and every threshold of its table reads it, so rows on any border of it fix the weight for all of them, and where the rows stand moves with every row written while the obligation does not. The same comparison read at two calls is two computations, each of which can weigh its positions wrongly on its own.

copies.description: Every copy of the comparison a call made that is cut at the same places, in the order they were read, each spelled the way a construct of a body and the calls it was made through are spelled everywhere else in the document. Calls cut at the same places are put to the same rows and are one computation.

position.description: The position whose weight is owed, as a path of the input.

outputCaseObligationId.description: What tells one case of a behavior's output from every other. The behavior and which case, and nothing about a position: an output has none, an axis is of an input, so there is no other account this could have an entry in and the array under `signature.output` is the one place it is kept. The behavior is part of it because two behaviors answering with the same sum owe that case separately.

behavior.description: The behavior whose output it is.

case.description: The case of that output, as the model declares it.

aRowThatDoesNotHold.description: A row that ran, or was to run, and did not do what it says: which row, where it is written, and where it stopped. The place and the stop travel with the row because a row covering an obligation of one behavior may be written for another, and a document narrowed to the first has no entry of that row to look them up in.

failedAt.description: Where the row stopped, which is not always the behavior answering otherwise. `input_fixture` is an input that could not be built and `expected_fixture` an expectation that could not be built, and neither applied the behavior; `fake_resolution` is a dependency with no fake for it; `ensures` is what the row states breaking what the behavior declares of its answer; `invocation` is the behavior applied and giving no answer; `comparison` is the behavior answering with something other than the row expects. What a row covers is what it reached before it stopped. A row that went over a budget or could not be handed over ends undecided and is not one of these.

whyKept.description: What kept a combination owed that no way of the body read whole reads. `a_function_read_as_a_whole` is a function whose ways were read as a whole and not one application at a time, which `shortfalls` says why of. `a_way_read_in_part` is a way holding a step the reading has no words for, which `shortOf` names. `a_decision_nothing_names` is a decision on a way whose subject no position names. `a_rule_no_decision_reads` is a rule the body wrote dividing `position` that no decision on its ways reads.

shortfalls.description: Each use of the function that is not an operation of the language applying it once to each element of a position of the input, read off the same uses the reading was judged from. `not_only_by_operations` is something other than an operation applying it: applied directly, handed to a function of the author's, kept in a value. `to_some_of_the_elements` is `operation` applying it only as far as `applied` says. `over_no_position` is `operation` applying it over a container that is no position of the input. A function two operations apply names only the one that falls short.

operation.description: The operation, as the author called it.

at.description: Where the function is written, where this document may say so.

position.description: The position the rule divides, as `axes` names it.

onlyWitnessedBy.description: The rows covering an obligation, written exactly where every one of them does not hold and absent wherever some other row covers it too. The obligation is met either way and counted as met: whatever a row that does not hold reached before it stopped, it reached. What this says is that the count has the obligation only through these rows — without them it is not covered. Correcting only the answer a row states leaves where it goes as it was, so that is not always what correcting it takes away. Another row is any row the measure counts that does not fail — one that held, one waiting for its answer, one recorded before there was a body — so an obligation without this field is not thereby one a row was seen to hold at.

rowObligationId.description: What tells one row an author wrote from every other, which is what the answer it owes is owed at. A key within this document: it names an entry of the behavior's `rowObligations`, and a consumer joins an `unanswered_row` finding to the row it is about on it. Three parts, because two of them are not enough: a row written with no name is numbered within the source that writes it, so a behavior exampled in a module and in a file attached to it has a first row in each. Not the arm such a row may stand at — an arm is owed a row and any row through it discharges that, while this is owed an answer and only an answer written here discharges it.

behavior.description: The behavior the row is written for.

name.description: The row's name, where it was written with one.

behavior.description: The behavior the row is written for.

ordinal.description: Which of its behavior's rows in that source it is, where it has no name.

classObligationId.description: What tells one class of one position from every other, which is not what a reader is shown. A key within this document: `axis` names an entry of `partition.axes` and `class` one of the strings that entry lists, and a consumer joins a finding to the class it is about on the pair. The words beside the finding are not a key — two positions of one behavior can divide into classes that read alike, and a consumer joining on those lands on whichever the walk wrote first. The axis names the behavior, so two behaviors dividing their own positions the same way are two of these.

class.description: Which class of that axis, as `partition.axes[].classes` lists it.

armObligationId.description: What tells one arm of a behavior from every other, which is not what a reader is shown. A key within this document: a consumer joins one run's arms against another run's on it. Neither `label` nor `at` is one — a body spliced in from out of sight has its copies at as many places as there are call sites, and two arms of two forks are both spelled `else`. Not a name anything outside one compilation can be matched by: `construct` is the reader's own count over what `definition` names, and what identity needs is that the numbering be a function of that definition's syntax and that no two constructs of it share a number — the definition and the number together are what tell one construct from every other, and two definitions' first constructs are two constructs. A document written before that count was kept within a definition carries no `definition` and counts the whole source instead.

module.description: The module whose source wrote the construct, which is what keeps a prelude helper's forks apart from those of the module expanding it.

definition.description: The definition whose source wrote the construct, present in a document whose `construct` is counted within one. A document written before construct numbering became a count within a definition has none, and its `construct` counts the whole source instead.

construct.description: Which construct of whatever `definition` names, by the reader's own count over it. Where `definition` is absent the document is an earlier one and this counts the constructs of the whole source.

lowered.description: Which fork of that construct, where a lowering makes more than one out of it — a comprehension's guards by their place in the list. Zero is the construct's own fork, which is every fork an author writes as one.

part.description: Which arm of the fork, by its place among the fork's arms.

decidedBy.description: What settles which rule this fork decides by, which is part of what one arm is. `the_declaration` is a fork that decides for itself, and every copy of it spliced into a body is one arm. `the_caller` is a fork whose declaration says the caller decides, and then it is one arm per rule a caller handed in — two of those are the same construct at the same place and are two things to cover. `not_said` is the same declaration where which rule reached here could not be worked out, and such an arm is `not_counted`.

rules.description: The rules the caller handed in, in the order the declaration names the parameters, present exactly where `decidedBy` is `the_caller`. A rule named at the call site is written as the declaration it names; a rule the source wrote out is written as the block of that source it is. Naming one declaration twice hands in one rule; writing the same expression twice is two.

declaration.description: The declaration a call site named. A declaration and never a binding: there are as many bindings as there are copies of the body that put the rule there.

module.description: The module whose source wrote the rule out, for a rule that has no name of its own.

block.description: Which block of whatever `writtenBy` names the rule is, by the reader's own count over that. Where `writtenBy` is absent the document is an earlier one and this counts the blocks of the whole source.

decision.description: The rules of the decision this behavior's body states, and which of them a row was seen taking. Beside `branch` and not among it: an arm is one branch the author wrote and a rule is one way through the body, so two rules can go through one arm. One entry per rule the reading of the body reached, whatever the rows did — a `decision_rule_uncovered` finding names one of these by its `obligationId`.

coverage.description: How far the reading of which rules the rows took got. Its own object because it is about the runs and the entries beside it are about the body: a build that read no row still states the rules it states.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. `not_asked` is a build that does not record where a run goes, which is a measure nobody made. The rest are a measure that was started and could not be finished, and each leaves what the rows take unknown rather than none: `the_body_was_not_read` is the model saying a body is written here and nothing having made it, `no_row_came_back` is rows written for this behavior that nothing could evaluate, `the_rows_carry_no_account` is rows that ran without the instrumentation a place is recorded by, and `no_rule_is_recognisable` is every rule of the body carrying a condition no run through it is recorded at or read with fewer conditions than its way consults. A behavior no row names is none of these: a reading over no rows was made, placed none and found no rule taken.

weakening.description: What the reading of the rules themselves went without, which is about this list rather than about any entry: a reading that stopped states the ways it reached and the rest are in no document.

waysNoInputTakes.description: The ways through the body the reading proved no input takes, apart from the rules: each is the conditions a way consulted and came out as, said of as few of them as still prove it, and stands for every rule that goes on from it — a rule consulting each of these conditions as the way did. None of those rules is in `obligations` and none is counted in `coverage`; a way here is not a rule however many rules it stands for, and no two of these stand one for the other. `because` is what the proof was had from: `the_conditions_on_the_way_clash` is conditions asking for two cases of one value, two answers of one truth or counts that leave none in common, whatever the numbers; `the_numbers_on_the_way_leave_none` is conditions that each leave values and leave none together once what the declarations hold is taken in with them. Absent where no way was proved one no input takes.

obligations.description: One entry per rule the body states.

allOf.description: What the composing came to is written exactly where a search of the rule had no candidate to try it with, which is the one answer it is about. Beside any other answer it would be a shortfall recorded of a search that composed a row and ran it.

taken.description: Whether a row was seen taking this rule. Absent where `coverage.status` is `unavailable`: a rule nothing was read about is not a rule no row takes, and `false` for both would be one word for two states.

weakening.description: What the reading of this rule went without, which is about this entry rather than about the list: `decision_rule_read_short` is a rule read with fewer of the distinctions its way consults than the body draws. No run is placed at such a rule and a finding about it refuses no build; a rule beside it without this word is not weakened by it. Absent where the rule was read in full.

requirement.description: Whether a row is owed at this rule at all, where something asked. `required` is a rule something was shown standing in, `excluded` is one the model leaves no value for — by a rule or by a type with too few values, which is not said here — and `unsettled` is this compiler having looked without finding — which is neither covered nor a gap and is owed no row. Absent where nothing asked: the question is put of the rules no row took, so a rule some row takes carries `taken` and no word here.

because.description: How the requirement came to that answer, at every place the rule is stated that answers it, each word once: a rule a helper states is searched at each call of the helper, and two calls may come to two answers. The places are every one of them where the model leaves each no row, and every one it leaves open otherwise, the one that established the most first; the first word is the requirement's own answer. Present with `requirement` except where that is `required`, whose answer is the row that was seen standing in and has nothing beside it. Five are the model's: `the_way_needs_one_position_to_be_two` is a way asking a position to be two things at once, `an_arm_nothing_reaches` a way through an arm no value arrives at, `a_comparison_outcome_nothing_reaches` a way needing a comparison to come out one way where nothing arrives coming out so — at every copy of it, where a helper is called more than once — `a_condition_never_comes_out_that_way` a way past a condition every row brings out the other way — a predicate that always holds, or sides whose difference is the same on every row — and `no_value_can_take_it` no value taking the way to the rule, whether the statements of numbers on the way leave none, which is read off the rules before anything is composed, or a search proves it, whether a rule or a type with too few values leaves none — a search takes every way of standing the dependencies in to say so. The rest are about the inquiry — a row was composed and took another rule, a row was composed against less than the way asks, a run this reading could not place, a run nothing watched, or there was nothing composed to try the rule with. `a_composed_row_was_short_of_the_way` is the one to read no negative from: the row was built and run, and a row meeting some of what the way states reaches whatever such a row reaches, so where it went says nothing about the rule. `nothing_was_composed_to_try` says only that the inquiry had no candidate; what the composing fell short on is `synthesisShortfalls`, a different question with a field of its own. A human report counts the rules under these rather than writing one line apiece, so this is what such a count is taken over.

reachProofsContradicted.description: The proofs that nothing arrives that would have left this rule no row before the rows ran, and that a row went against — which is why it was asked at all. Each is an entry of the behavior's `reachProofsContradicted`, written the same way, so a consumer joins the two and counts a proof once however many rules rested on it. Never a `way_no_input_takes`: no rule of the decision is past such a way. Present only beside a `requirement` other than `excluded`: a rule still excluded is excluded by something that stands, whatever was taken back on its way. Absent where no such proof was on its way.

synthesisShortfalls.description: What this compiler's composings came to where none produced a candidate for the rule, one entry per word they came back with, present exactly where `because` holds `nothing_was_composed_to_try`. Over every place of the rule that had nothing to try, since this document does not tell the places apart. This compiler's shortfall and never an answer about the model: a way nothing here composed a value for may be the easiest row in the file to write by hand, so whether a row is owed at the rule stays `unsettled` rather than settled by this. A rule is composed for once per way of standing its dependencies in, and every way that had nothing to try is here; two ways that came back with one word are one entry holding what both met, and two entries with one `reason` differ in their `causes`. In one order, whatever order the ways were walked in.

reason.description: What the composing came to, in the vocabulary every search of this compiler answers in rather than one written for rules.

figures.description: The figures of this compiler's that stopped the searches with this word. Each is a number an author could raise, and `reason` beside it is the answer of a search that did not finish. In one order, whatever order the searches met them in. Absent where no figure stopped one.

planCut.description: The figures of this compiler's that cut short the plan the searches with this word ran over, or left them no plan to run over. Not figures that stopped a search: such a search ran to the end of what it was handed, or was never made, and `reason` beside it is about less than the rule's way had. Each is a number an author could raise. In one order, whatever order the searches met them in. Absent where every search ran over the whole of the way.

populations.description: What this compiler writes some of rather than all of, where the searches with this word walked such a population in part. Not a number: raising a figure does not reach the rest, which is work this compiler has not done. In one order, whatever order the searches met them in. Absent where no population was walked in part.

unheld.description: The numbers the searches with this word could not hold: what was being worked out, and why the number was not held — `more_room_could_answer` is a host with more room reaching it, `no_representation_exists` is a number nothing here represents. Absent where every number was held.

causes.description: Why the values this compiler had to try were not shown to be every value the declarations leave, one entry per thing that gave the offer none — which says the offer was not shown to be exhaustive, and not that a value was left untried. Beside `reason` and never inside it: that word is what the search came to and these are what it was given to work with, and a consumer reading the word alone counts a rule this compiler never read as a rule the values were refused by. Absent where nothing kept the offer from being every value the declarations leave, which is what an entry carrying a word for the search and no array here says.

allOf.description: A rule is named exactly where the shortfall is attributed to one. Written as a shape and not only as a sentence: what the declarations leave between them is nobody's rule and the allowance for composing a value is about no rule of the position, so an entry carrying one under either would send an author to a rule that reads perfectly — and an entry attributed to a rule and naming none would leave them every rule written at the position to look at.

And what stopped it is one of the two, never both and never neither. They are two vocabularies rather than two words: a reading that stopped is a rule somebody may write another way and a limit is a figure, and an entry carrying both would be one thing that gave nothing wearing two accounts of why.

position.description: Where in the row the values were being composed for, in the terms a row is written in.

attribution.description: What the shortfall is attributed to, which is what decides where an author goes about it. `a_rule` is one they wrote and may rewrite; `the_rules_together` is what two of them leave between them, which is nobody's rule and a size this compiler declined to work out; `composing_a_value` is the allowance for working out a value at all, which is about no rule of the position.

rule.description: How a reader finds the rule that gave the offer no value, present exactly where `attribution` is `a_rule`. The same handle a `notRead` entry carries for the same rule. Not what tells one rule from another: `ruleId` beside this is.

ruleId.description: Which rule the entry is about, present exactly with `rule`.

unread.description: What stopped the reading of it, where what gave nothing was a reading that stopped. Words `notRead` writes, so a rule reported unread here and the same rule reported unread under the position are one piece of news rather than two. Present exactly where `limit` is absent.

limit.description: Which limit refused it, where a limit did. `a_machine_larger_than_one_may_be` is a pattern that can be written smaller; `what_composing_a_value_may_spend` is an allowance already spent, which the same pattern asked for first would not have met; `what_one_pattern_may_spend` is the allowance the pattern a rule states is built under, spent on that pattern alone, which a smaller pattern would not run past whatever else was asked; it is written only where `attribution` is `a_rule`. Present exactly where `unread` is absent, and no reading stopped: the rule was read from end to end.

interaction.description: The combinations of decisions this behavior's body settles one value by, and which of them a row was seen making. Beside `decision` and not among it: a rule is one way through the body and a combination is one meeting on it, so a row through every way can leave a combination unmade. The combinations a row was seen making are listed under `obligations`, and the ones none was seen making are stated under `groups` as the sets of choices they come to, so that what is written grows with the decisions and not with the ways they come out. Present exactly where the body's decisions meet, which is where `partition.pairs` is absent.

coverage.description: How far the reading of which combinations the rows made got. Its own object because it is about the runs and the entries beside it are about the body: a build that read no row still states the combinations it states.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. `not_asked` is a build that does not record where a run goes, which is a measure nobody made. The rest are a measure that was started and could not be finished, and each leaves what the rows make unknown rather than none: `no_row_came_back` is rows written for this behavior and none of them coming back to be read, and `the_rows_carry_no_account` is rows that ran without the instrumentation a place is recorded by.

groupsNotMeasured.description: How many groups of this body's decisions were wider than the measure walks. What they hold is combinations nobody counted, so a consumer reading the entries below as the whole of what the body has is told here that it is not.

made.description: Whether a row was seen making this combination. Absent where the coverage has no number: a combination nothing was read about is not one no row makes.

obligations.description: One entry per combination a row was seen making, with the rows. Empty where the coverage has no number: nothing says which a row made, and one entry for each combination the body has would be one for each choice of each group, as many as the factors multiplied out. What the body has is under `groups`, and the combinations no row makes are the sets of choices there.

groups.description: The groups of this body's decisions that were walked, whatever was read of the rows, and where something was the combinations of each that no row makes. Absent where the body has no group the measure walked.

interactionGroup.description: One group of a body's decisions: the decisions that settle one value together. A group is its way in and its factors, a factor being one decision of the body with the outcomes it can come out as, and a choice of the group is one outcome of each factor. The combinations of the group are its choices that leave every position something, so a group can hold fewer choices than the product of its factors. A group is written whether or not anything was read of the rows, and `unobserved` states the choices no row makes as sets where something was, which is how what is written grows with the factors and not with the choices.

group.description: Which of the body's groups this is, counted from zero in the order the measure met them. What an `interaction_uncovered` finding's `pattern` names, and the same for the same model whichever rows are written.

wayIn.description: The decisions every choice of the group is under: what the path to the meeting settles. Empty where the group is the first thing the body settles.

factors.description: The factors of the group, in the order a pattern's `fixed` is written in.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the factor can come out as, in the order a pattern's `fixed` counts them from zero; each is the decisions that outcome settles.

choices.description: How many choices the group has that leave every position something: its combinations. Not the product of its factors' outcomes where some choices leave a position nothing.

unobserved.description: Present exactly where the coverage has a number, and empty where every choice was made. The choices of the group no row makes, as sets that cover each of them once. Two choices are in one set only where the findings about them stand alike: what the reading went without and what is open about whether a row can be written are never mixed.

combinations.description: How many choices of the group are in the set.

obligationId.description: Which combination of the body it is, present exactly where the set holds one choice. A set of more is not a combination and has no identity of its own beyond its group and `fixed`.

patternFixed.description: The outcome a set of choices takes at each factor of its group, in the order of the group's `factors`: the position of the outcome among the factor's `outcomes`, or null where the set holds the factor either way.

branch.description: Which arms of the behavior's body the rows go through. Branch-arm coverage, not path coverage: going through both arms of two nested conditions says nothing about their combinations.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. The first two are a behavior with no arm to measure at all rather than arms nothing measured, and no row would give it one: `no_body` is a `>->` composition or a behavior with no `let`, and `no_arm_obligations` is a body that owes no arm — one that forks nowhere a row can be in or out of, or whose every fork the model's own rules prove nothing arrives at. Both are claims about what the model says. The rest are a behavior that does owe arms: `not_asked` is a build that did not ask for them; `unreadable` is a run whose instrumentation could not be tied back to the body; `no_rows` is a behavior no row names; `body_was_not_read` is the model saying a body is written here and the image this run was measured in not carrying it, so what the behavior owes was not read — named for the absence rather than for any of the ways an image comes to be without a body, which nothing here can tell apart. It is what `no_body` used to be answered with, and the two are a claim about the model and a claim about this image. `bodies_not_elaborated` is what documents before it said, quantified over the module rather than over the behavior; nothing writes it now.

denominatorSettled.description: Whether the arms below are all the arms this behavior owes a row for. Which arms it owes is worked out from the model's own proofs about what can reach what: an arm nothing arrives at is instrumented — a probe is what would show such a proof wrong — and is not owed, because no row can light it. False where a row went through one of those anyway: nothing about the model is wrong there and the proof is, so the arms stand where they stand and what is in doubt is the set they are counted out of. Present exactly where `obligations` is, since it qualifies that array. Which proof it was is `weakening`, as `proof_contradicted`.

obligations.description: Every arm this behavior is owed a row for, one entry per arm the author wrote rather than per occurrence of it: a helper spliced under three call sites has its arms counted once, and an arm the model's own rules prove nothing reaches is not owed and is not here. The canonical form of this measure and the only place an arm's state is written: how many arms there are and how many a row goes through are folds of this array, and `disposition` is what each arm came to. Present exactly where the measurement has a value, which is where `status` is `complete` or `partial`. A behavior with no arms to measure has no array here rather than an empty one — read as one, a measure that does not apply would divide into a covered count of zero and answer a question nobody put.

allOf.description: An arm says where it stands once, and beside it whatever left it open. `undecided` is the reading that stopped, so it carries `weakening`; `not_counted` is the fork nothing tells apart, so it carries `notCountedBecause`; the two settled states are settled by the rows and carry neither. Nothing here re-encodes the disposition: a status and a hit beside it would be the same answer twice, free to disagree with the first.

disposition.description: Where this arm stands in the account. `met` is a row goes through it; `unmet` is no row does and every row was read, which is the one state a build refuses over and the one a finding of kind `arm_unreached` is made of; `undecided` is no row was seen to and a reading that could have been holding one did not run to the end, which is counted and is never a finding; `not_counted` is an arm outside the two numbers, with `notCountedBecause` saying why. The first three make a partition of what the count holds, so a consumer that folds them has said what the difference between the numbers is.

notCountedBecause.description: Why this arm is outside the count, present exactly where `disposition` is `not_counted`. `occurrences_not_told_apart` is a fork whose declaration says the caller decides where which rule that was could not be worked out: one place can stand for as many arms as there are rules reaching it, so a row through it may or may not be a row through this one. Both arms of such a fork are out together, and `weakening` says `arms_unsettled`.

weakening.description: What the reading of this behavior's rows went without, present exactly where `disposition` is `undecided`. It is why nobody can say whether a row goes through this arm — a row that could have gone through it did not come back — and not a second way of saying that nobody can: what the arm came to is `disposition`, and it is said once.

kind.description: What this way through the construct is. `then` and `else` are the arms of an `if`; `continued` is the body past a `guard` whose condition held, which the author writes no word for; `kept` and `dropped` are the element a comprehension yields and the empty list it yields instead; `case` is an arm of a `match`; `constructed` and `departure` are the two ways out of an attempted construction. Read beside `construct`: the same outcome under two constructs is two things, and an `else` written under a `guard` is not the `else` of an `if`.

construct.description: What the author wrote this an outcome of. The meaning of an arm is the pair: an `else` written under an `if` and one written under a `guard` are the same outcome of two constructs, and a consumer told only the outcome cannot tell them apart.

partition.description: How much of what the model distinguishes about this behavior's inputs the rows reach. Absent where there were no positions to write: the positions here are the ones the model divides, worked out from the behavior's boundary and the rules written about it, and no declaration gives them — so a boundary that did not work out leaves nothing to divide and an empty `axes` would say the model divides none of them. Said as `behavior_boundary_not_derived` in the behavior's `weakening`. A `>->` composition is not this — it is measured at its stages and carries a section saying so.

axesMeasure.description: Whether the positions were measured at all, which the `axes` array cannot say: an empty one is what a behavior with no position to divide has and what a behavior whose positions could not be read has.

reason.description: Why there is no measure, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. `the_reading_did_not_run_out` is a reading that produced no position and was short of something it answers for, so the model is not thereby known to divide none; `nothing_is_divided` is a reading that answered everything it answers for and found no position the model divides, which no row would change; `no_feasible_input` is the declarations leaving the behavior no value to be measured at all, so this measure has no subject rather than having found none — a class is a set of values a row can be written at, and there are none; `no_subject` is a behavior with no positions of its own, a `>->` composition, which is measured at its stages. `body_was_not_read` is a behavior whose body the image this run was made in does not carry: what its own rules say was never asked, so the classes here are what the declarations and the clauses came to and the measure is short of a reading rather than short of nothing. Told apart from the first because that one is a reading that was made and stopped on something it can name, and this one names nothing. `no_axis_derived` is what the first was called while it also stood for the second, and is retired rather than gone.

boundariesMeasure.description: The same for the lines. An empty `boundaries` array is what a model with no bound has and what a model whose bounds the reading could not reach has.

reason.description: Why there is no measure, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. `the_reading_did_not_run_out` is a reading that produced no line and was short of something it answers for, so the model is not thereby known to draw none; `no_rule_draws_a_line` is a reading that answered everything it answers for and found no rule drawing a line, which no row would change since a row cannot make a line; `no_feasible_input` is the declarations leaving the behavior no value to be measured at all, so this measure has no subject rather than having found no rule — a line is a place rows part, and there are no rows to part; `no_subject` is a behavior with no positions of its own. `body_was_not_read` is the same of this measure: one rule of a body draws a line at every number it names, so a behavior whose body this run's image does not carry is short of that reading rather than known to draw no line. `no_lines_derived` is what the first was called while it also stood for the second, and is retired rather than gone.

path.description: The input position, as a parameter and the fields read off it. A newtype's `value` is never a step.

read.description: How far this measure got with the rules about this position. It qualifies `classes` and nothing else says it: a rule nothing took in may yet refuse a value one of the classes holds, so `classes` is the denominator the model states and not one every member of which is known to stand. The questions themselves are in `unanswered` beside the measures — the model raises them and every measure here is one reader of them, so a position no axis came back for still has whatever was written about it. This says only whether the questions *this* measure answers were answered: which values may stand somewhere is what classes are made of, and where a line falls is the border measure's, counted there.

extent.description: Whether anything this measure reads about this position is left standing: a rule out of sight, or a question about which values may stand here that nothing answered. `partial` where either holds. A question about where the values stop does not make this `partial` — it is not this measure's to answer, and counting it here would put back a number `partition` and `border` were separated into.

rulesNotReached.description: The walk never reached some of the rules written about this position, so what is written there is not known. Written only where that is so. Its own axis beside the questions and not exclusive with them: a rule can have arrived and gone unaccounted for while a subtree beside it was never entered, and both are said.

classes.description: The classes a row can be written at: what the model divides this position into, less what its own rules refuse.

use.description: Whether anything the behavior states — its body or a clause of it — reads the value at this position. `not_read` only where every one of them was read and none reads the value, a field beside it being read off the value it sits under not reading it. A row is owed at each of `classes` unless this is `not_read`, where a row at one class gives the answer a row at any other gives. `classes` and `covered` are the same either way. Not whether the body tells the classes apart: a value copied into the answer is `read`.

excluded.description: Classes the position's own rules refuse, that the body also answers `unreachable` for. Out of `classes` because no value of one can be constructed, and named here because the type still has them.

reasons.description: The reasons written at the `unreachable`s this class leads to — one, unless several paths abort for different reasons.

unprovenClaims.description: Classes the body answers `unreachable` for that nothing settled. Still in `classes` and still owed a row: what removes an obligation is a proof, and a row written at one may reach the `unreachable` and be refused.

reasons.description: The reasons written at the `unreachable`s this class leads to.

coveredOnlyBy.description: The classes of `covered` only rows that do not hold are in, each beside those rows. Written exactly where there is one.

reason.description: Why there is no number, present exactly where `status` is `unavailable`. A behavior no row names was not measured here, so the classes nothing sits in are not classes nothing reaches. `not_asked` is a build that asked for no measurement at all, which reads no row anywhere.

weights.description: What each computation of a value derived from several positions is owed where the rule cuts it at several places, as a table of thresholds cuts the value it is looked up by: a weight for each position, in place of the classes the thresholds would have divided it into. One entry per position of each computation, and a computation is one comparison as one call of it reads it, so the same comparison read at two calls is two computations. Beside `boundaries` and not under them, because a computation is owed its weights whether or not a border of it was drawn. A `tilt_of_a_derived_value_not_shown` finding joins to the entry carrying its `obligationId`. Absent where no computation is cut at several places.

standing.description: `shown`: the rows beside the borders of the computation fix the weight of this position, which is where some row fails a computation weighing it one more and some row fails one weighing it one less. `not_shown`: they do not, so rows that fix it are owed and a finding names it. `undecided`: nothing was read against the computation, a border of it was not read and the rest leave the weight unfixed, or the exact arithmetic gave out on a row, which is no claim that the rows fix nothing and is no finding.

besides.description: What this line is owed as a line: one obligation per line of its fault family — the lines weighing one of its positions one more or one less — and where each stands. A `boundary_not_told_from_another` finding joins to one of these. Apart from the ids under `items`: those are owed at places on the line and there are four of them, and these are the line itself held against each line beside it, because what a row answering one shows is which of two lines the model draws. The family is the model's own and no row moves it, so the same entries are here before the rows rule a line out as after; what changes is `standing`. Empty where the line has no family, or where the question could not be put of it at all, which the measure's weakening says. The same on every entry for one line of the model read at several positions, since what such a line is owed does not depend on where it was read; `lineId` is what tells those entries apart.

standing.description: `ruled_out`: no threshold on that line keeps every row the model keeps and refuses every row it refuses. `stands`: some threshold does, so a row ruling it out is owed and a finding names it. `undecided`: the question was put and could not be settled — a row nothing watched, one whose values could not be read, a sum the exact arithmetic could not hold, or no input a row arrives at — which weakens the measure and is never read as ruled out. `not_due`: a row is not yet at every point of the border, and the line is asked about once one is. `not_applicable`: the model leaves no value on the side the border refuses — every point it has there is excluded because no value can stand there — so no row could rule the line out whatever threshold it is drawn at, and none is owed; keeping values on the right side of the line is the model's guarantee, made by a type that has no such value or by a rule checked at construction, and not something a row could show.

lineId.description: Which line this entry is, and what an entry of `keptOpenBy` about a line names it by. One entry per `lineId`.

origin.description: The rule that drew this line, as a `ruleHandle`, and after it the declarations that took an end of the line in where any did. The handle alone where none did, which is what the `obligations` entry for a point of this line carries. Not itself a handle, because those words are about the line rather than about the rule; what a consumer keys on is the `ruleId` under that entry.

kind.description: What this line is a line at. `at_value` is a place of the position `axis` names, which is what an invariant's bound and a guard against a constant draw. `between_positions` is a guard comparing one position against another: the line is where the two hold the same place, `axis` names the left of it and `value` the other position rather than a value. `over_a_form` is a rule over an arithmetic form across several positions: the line is where the form comes to `value`, `axis` names the form as an author would write it and `value` is a number the form takes rather than a value any position holds. `remainder_of_a_form` is a rule over what a division by a written number leaves of a form of several positions: `axis` names the call as `Int.floorMod(form, divisor)` and `value` is the remainder, from nought to one below the divisor. `remainder_by_an_input` is a rule over what one whole number of one position leaves of another divided by a whole number of another position: `axis` names the call as `Int.floorMod(a, b)` and `value` is the remainder, below the divisor in size and of its sign. `product_of_two` is a rule over what two whole numbers of two positions come to multiplied: `axis` names the product as `a * b` and `value` is the product. `count_of_elements` is a rule over how many elements of a container meet something: the line is where that many do, `axis` names the count as `#container [statement]` and `value` is the number of elements. `count_of_different_values` is a rule over how many different values the elements of a container meeting something hold at one place of each, two elements holding one value counted once: the line is where that many values are held, `axis` names the count as `#different container [place] where [statement]` and `value` is the number of values. Reading `value` without reading this reads a position's name as a value.

value.description: Where the line is, as an author would write it: a value where `kind` is `at_value`; the other position, and how far from it where the rule holds them apart, where it is `between_positions`; a number the form comes to where it is `over_a_form`; how many elements where it is `count_of_elements`; and how many values where it is `count_of_different_values`. Not what any one of the border's points asks for — three of the four ask for something else, and each says so itself.

items.description:
The coverage items this border owes, keyed on the border the way the technique keys them (ISTQB CTAL-TA v4.0 §3.1.1). One per point the line has and each exactly once, told apart by `location`: a rule that orders the values has four, and a rule that names a value has five — the value it names, the nearest value on each side of it, and the run either way. How many of them a border owes a row at is the rule's answer and not a constant, so a point it owes none at carries `notOwed` rather than being left out; a document short of one would read as this compiler being short of an item the technique asks for.

Every border has a value against the line inside it and one outside it, so an `on` and an `off` are always here. The other two roles are not: a rule that names a value puts both its runs in one class, so `x == 10` has two `out` items and no `in`, and `x /= 10` the other way about.

oneOf.description: A point no row is owed at carries which point it is and why, and nothing else. Closed rather than listing what it may not have: the list was the keys of the owed side written a second time, and a field added to that side was a field somebody had to remember to forbid here. Two went unforbidden that way — `weakening`, which no measurement of a point owing no row can produce, and `writableBecause`, which is evidence about a row nobody is owed.

A point whose own place on the order a model's own decimals put far enough apart in scale that the exact arithmetic could not read: neither owed nor refused, and nothing else here says which it would have been.

allOf.description: The verdict and the grounds are one answer written twice, so this says they cannot differ. Where the array is there and `knownWritable` is `true`, some ground is in it.

And where it is there and `knownWritable` is `false`, none is. Both are conditional on the array being present, because an absent one is a producer that predates it rather than a point with no grounds.

point.description: Which of the four coverage items of this border this entry is, in the words domain testing gives them. `on` is inside the equivalence partition the border bounds and closest to it, `off` is outside it and closest to it, `in` is inside it and away from it, and `out` is outside it and away from it. Which one the line's own value serves as turns on whether the border is closed or open, so the same place is the `on` point of `x <= 100` and the `off` point of `x < 100`. Not what tells one item of a border from another: two of them can carry one of these words, and `location` is what they differ by.

notOwed.description: Why no row is owed here, present exactly when one is not. `no_value_can_stand_there` is the model's own answer — nothing outside an invariant's bound can be constructed, so the points out there are excluded and counted out, a side one value wide has no `in` point for the same reason, and a count of a `Set<Bool>` past two has no value with no rule written. The word says that no value stands at the point and not what showed it: a type with few values, a rule on the type, a rule on a container's size and how many of an element's values meet a statement each show it, and two of them may show one point alike. `the_carrier_names_no_neighbour` is this language having no name for the value one step from the line, which a `Decimal`, a `DateTime` and a `String` do not — at a place, and at the difference two terms of a line between them stand at. The two ask different things of a reader — one is the model having settled the point and the other is a limit of this language — which is why the key is a word and not a flag.

stops.description: Where else the point was settled, present exactly when `notOwed` is: the far end of the empty run beside the line, or an end the rules leave the position at that refuses the value, each written as an obligation's `stops` is. Empty where the line alone settled it. With the line and `location` it is what tells this point from the same place of the same line left out elsewhere, and what a consumer joins it to `declarations[].excluded[].pointId` by. A set: the order carries no meaning.

relation.description: How a row here has to stand to what `against` names: `=` for a place, `in` for a run of the quantity's values, `/=` for every value but one. Present exactly where a row is owed. Two of the four items ask for a place and two ask for a run of values, so `against` is read together with this: under `=` and `/=` it is a value, and under `in` it is the run written whole. A document carrying a value for all four would name a witness of a run as though it were the run. `<` and `>` were written here by compilers that read a point away from the line as everything past it rather than as the partition the border bounds; a run is written under `in` now.

against.description: What that relation is against, as an author would write it. Under `=` and `/=` it is one value: a value of the position where the border's `kind` is `at_value`; the other position, stepped where the point is not where the two meet, where it is `between_positions`; and a number the form comes to where it is `over_a_form`. Under `in` it is a run of the quantity's values written whole — `10 < n <= 20` — because a run has two ends and one of them alone would name a value inside it as though it were the run.

hit.description: Whether a row this coverage measurement read stands at the point. Present exactly where the measurement has a value, which is where `status` is `complete` or `partial`. `false` is what the measurement found — no row that could be read is at the point — and never stands for a measurement that was not made or could not be finished: those have no answer here and the key is absent. Under `partial` the `false` is over what was observed, and `weakening` beside it says why that is not a complete absence.

knownWritable.description: Whether anything has shown that a row can be written at this point: `true` where at least one ground established it, `false` where none did. `false` never says the point cannot be written at — what says that is the border refusing to owe a row at the point at all, which is `notOwed`. Which grounds hold is `writableBecause`, and the causes of there being none are not listed here: each belongs to the evidence its ground comes from, and a list of them written into this sentence is one that goes stale whenever any of them moves. This is its own body of evidence and not this measurement's answer, so it is written whether or not the coverage measurement has a value: a point nobody measured whose rules prove it inhabited carries `true` beside a `status` of `unavailable`, and the two are consistent.
